questions.explanation: The French writer Montesquieu, in The Spirit of the Laws (1748), argued that liberty is safest when making, executing and interpreting laws are done by separate organs of government.

whyNot.C: Dicey is associated with the rule of law.
whyNot.A: Lincoln is associated with a famous definition of democracy.
whyNot.B: Weber is associated with bureaucracy.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which arm of government interprets the law and settles disputes?
questions.explanation: Government has three arms: the legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out, and the judiciary (the courts) interprets them and settles disputes.

whyNot.A: The legislature makes laws.
whyNot.C: The executive implements laws.
whyNot.D: The civil service is part of the executive and implements policies.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: In Nigeria, citizens elect members of the House of Representatives to make laws on their behalf. This is an example of
questions.explanation: In representative (indirect) democracy, citizens choose representatives in periodic elections who then make decisions for them. Large modern states use this because all citizens cannot meet together to make laws.

whyNot.A: In direct democracy, citizens make decisions themselves, as in ancient Athens.
whyNot.B: Military rule is government by soldiers who were not elected.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following helps to protect the independence of the judiciary in Nigeria?
options: Making judges hold office for only two years
Election of judges by political parties
Allowing the President to remove any judge at will
Judges' security of tenure, with their salaries charged on the Consolidated Revenue Fund
questions.explanation: Judges can only be removed for specific reasons through a set procedure (security of tenure), and their salaries are charged directly on the Consolidated Revenue Fund, so the executive or legislature cannot cut them to punish judges. This lets judges decide cases without fear.

whyNot.B: Party election would make judges depend on politicians.
whyNot.C: Removal at will would make judges fear the President.
whyNot.A: Very short tenure would make judges insecure and easier to pressure.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: People in a proposed new state are asked to vote "yes" or "no" directly on whether the state should be created. This method of popular participation is called
questions.explanation: A referendum is a direct vote by the electorate on a specific question or proposal. Section 8 of the Constitution requires a referendum among the people of the area for the creation of a new state.

whyNot.D: Recall is the removal of an elected representative by the voters.
whyNot.A: A by-election fills a vacant seat.
whyNot.B: Lobbying is persuading lawmakers, not a vote by citizens.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Why is a free press important in a democracy?
options: It informs citizens and exposes abuse of power so leaders can be held accountable
It allows government to control what citizens think
It replaces the need for elections
It makes laws when the legislature is on recess
questions.explanation: A free press gives citizens accurate information on public affairs and reports wrongdoing by officials. Informed citizens can then vote wisely and demand accountability, which is the heart of democracy.

whyNot.B: Government control of opinion is a feature of authoritarian rule, not a free press.
whyNot.C: The press supports elections; it cannot replace them.
whyNot.D: The press has no law-making power.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: On election day, a politician gives voters ₦5,000 each at a polling unit to vote for him. This electoral malpractice is called
questions.explanation: Vote buying is offering money or gifts to voters to influence how they vote. It is an offence under the Electoral Act and undermines free and fair elections.

whyNot.B: Lobbying is persuading lawmakers or officials about policies.
whyNot.C: Canvassing is lawfully asking people for their votes, usually by explaining one's programme.
whyNot.D: Campaign financing is the lawful raising and spending of money for a campaign.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Under section 143 of the 1999 Constitution, a resolution to remove the President from office by impeachment must finally be supported by at least
options: two-thirds of the members of each House of the National Assembly
one-half of the members of the House of Representatives only
a simple majority of the Senate only
three-quarters of all State Houses of Assembly
questions.explanation: After a panel investigates and finds the allegations proved, each House of the National Assembly must adopt the report by a resolution supported by at least two-thirds of all its members. Only then is the President removed.

whyNot.C: Both Houses must vote, and a simple majority is not enough.
whyNot.D: State Houses of Assembly do not take part in impeaching the President.
whyNot.B: Both Houses are involved, with a two-thirds requirement.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Some decrees made by past military governments in Nigeria contained "ouster clauses". How did these clauses undermine the rule of law?
options: They gave citizens more rights than the Constitution
They made judges' salaries higher than ministers'
They required all laws to be passed by elected legislators
They stopped the courts from examining or challenging actions taken under the decrees
questions.explanation: An ouster clause removes (ousts) the jurisdiction of the courts over a matter. Under military rule, such clauses meant citizens could not go to court to challenge government actions, so the government was effectively above the law.

whyNot.A: Ouster clauses reduced, not increased, citizens' protection.
whyNot.C: Military regimes ruled by decree, without elected legislators.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: World AIDS Day, set aside to raise awareness about HIV and AIDS, is marked every year on
questions.explanation: World AIDS Day is held on 1 December each year to raise awareness about HIV, remember those who have died and show support for people living with HIV.

whyNot.D: 10 December is Human Rights Day.
whyNot.A: 26 June is the International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking.
whyNot.C: 30 July is the World Day against Trafficking in Persons.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a secret cult in a Nigerian school?
options: A religious fellowship that meets openly for worship
A registered students' union that represents all students
A departmental association that organises academic seminars
A group whose membership, rituals and activities are hidden and which often uses violence and intimidation
questions.explanation: Secret cults keep their members, oaths and activities secret and often use violence, intimidation and crime. They are banned in schools, and section 38(4) of the Constitution forbids membership of a secret society.

whyNot.B: A students' union is open and lawful.
whyNot.C: Departmental associations are open academic bodies.
whyNot.A: Open religious fellowships are not secret societies.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: What is the surest way for an unmarried teenager to avoid getting HIV through sexual contact?
options: Avoiding shaking hands with infected people
questions.explanation: Abstinence (not having sex) removes the risk of sexual transmission of HIV completely. It is the safest choice for young unmarried people.

whyNot.C: Antibiotics act against bacteria; HIV is a virus.
whyNot.A: HIV is not spread by handshakes.
whyNot.D: A good diet supports health but does not prevent HIV infection.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Long-term use of Indian hemp (cannabis) by young people is linked to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Heavy and long-term cannabis use, especially when it begins in adolescence, is linked to mental health problems including psychosis, as well as poor memory and declining school performance.

whyNot.B: Cannabis use harms memory and concentration.
whyNot.D: Drug abuse usually lowers academic performance.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Some young women from a Nigerian town are promised hairdressing jobs in Europe. On arrival, their passports are seized and they are forced into prostitution to pay "debts". What crime has been committed against them?
questions.explanation: Human trafficking is recruiting or moving people by deception, force or coercion for exploitation. The young women were deceived with false job offers and then sexually exploited, with their documents seized to control them.

whyNot.D: Legal migration involves genuine jobs and the person's free choice; there was deception and exploitation here.
whyNot.B: Kidnapping for ransom aims to collect payment from the victim's family for release.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a common reason why some students join secret cults?
options: Peer pressure and the desire for protection or power
questions.explanation: Students often join cults because of pressure from friends, a wish to feel powerful or protected, or the promise of influence. Schools and counsellors work against cultism, and it has nothing to do with graduation requirements.

whyNot.C: School authorities ban and fight cultism.
whyNot.B: Guidance counsellors warn students against cults.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Students in a class refuse to eat with a classmate living with HIV. Why is their behaviour wrong?
options: HIV is not spread by sharing meals, and such stigma harms the classmate
Sharing meals is the main way HIV spreads, so they should report her instead
People living with HIV are not allowed to attend school
Only teachers may decide who eats with whom
questions.explanation: HIV is not transmitted through casual contact like eating together. Stigma and discrimination hurt people living with HIV, discourage others from getting tested and break the right to freedom from discrimination.

whyNot.B: HIV is not spread through sharing food.
whyNot.C: People living with HIV have the same right to education as everyone else.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: In which year was the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) established?
questions.explanation: The NDLEA was established by Decree No. 48 of 1989 (now the NDLEA Act) to fight the production, trafficking and abuse of illegal drugs in Nigeria.

whyNot.A: 1979 is the year of the Second Republic constitution.
whyNot.D: 1999 is the year the current Constitution came into force.
whyNot.B: 2003 is the year NAPTIP was established.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: How can the transmission of HIV from an infected mother to her baby be greatly reduced?
options: The baby is given extra vitamins at birth
The mother takes antiretroviral drugs during pregnancy and breastfeeding
The mother avoids all contact with health workers
The mother takes antibiotics only after delivery
questions.explanation: Mother-to-child transmission can occur during pregnancy, delivery or breastfeeding. When the mother takes antiretroviral therapy throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding (with the baby also given preventive medicine), the risk of passing HIV to the baby falls to a very low level.

whyNot.D: Antibiotics do not act on HIV.
whyNot.A: Vitamins do not stop HIV transmission.
whyNot.C: Antenatal care is essential for preventing transmission.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Section 38(4) of the 1999 Constitution says that nothing in that section entitles any person to form, take part in the activity of, or be a member of a secret society. Which right does section 38 itself protect?
options: Right to peaceful assembly and association
Freedom of expression and the press
Freedom of thought, conscience and religion
questions.explanation: Section 38 guarantees freedom of thought, conscience and religion, including the freedom to change and practise one's religion. Subsection (4) makes clear that this freedom does not cover secret societies, so cult membership has no constitutional protection.

whyNot.C: Freedom of expression is in section 39.
whyNot.B: Peaceful assembly and association is in section 40.
whyNot.A: Freedom from discrimination is in section 42.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: A civil servant in a federal ministry openly campaigns for a political party during office hours. Which principle of the civil service is he breaking?
questions.explanation: Neutrality requires civil servants to serve any government in power faithfully without taking sides in party politics. Campaigning for a party during office hours breaks this principle.

whyNot.D: Anonymity is about civil servants not taking public credit or blame for policies.
whyNot.A: Permanence is about keeping one's job when governments change.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Who is the most senior career officer of the Federal Civil Service of Nigeria?
options: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
questions.explanation: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation is the most senior career civil servant. He or she leads the federal civil service, advises on personnel matters and coordinates the permanent secretaries.

whyNot.B: The Chief Justice heads the judiciary.
whyNot.A: The Senate President heads the Senate, part of the legislature.
whyNot.D: The Attorney-General is the chief law officer and a minister.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is part of civil society?
options: A non-governmental organisation that runs literacy classes for women
questions.explanation: Civil society is made up of organised groups outside government and business, such as NGOs, community associations, religious bodies, professional bodies and trade unions. An NGO running literacy classes is part of civil society.

whyNot.A: A ministry is part of government.
whyNot.D: The police are a government security agency.
whyNot.C: A local government council is the third tier of government.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: The Nigeria Union of Teachers mainly works to protect the welfare and working conditions of its own members. What type of pressure group is it?
questions.explanation: Interest or protective groups defend the interests of a section of society, usually their own members, such as workers or professionals. Promotional or cause groups campaign for a cause that benefits the wider public, such as the environment or human rights.

whyNot.D: A promotional group works for a general cause, not mainly for its own members' welfare.
whyNot.B: The NUT does not contest elections to form government.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: After a general election brings a new government to power, the civil servants in the ministries remain at their posts. Which feature of the civil service does this show?
questions.explanation: Permanence means civil servants are career officials who stay in office regardless of changes in government. This gives continuity, so the work of government goes on smoothly.

whyNot.D: Anonymity is about civil servants staying out of the public eye.
whyNot.A: Neutrality is about not taking sides in politics; it helps explain why they can stay, but staying on is permanence.
whyNot.C: Red tape is a problem of delay, not a feature.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Apart from implementing government policies, which of these is a function of senior civil servants?
options: Advising ministers on policy using their experience and records
questions.explanation: Senior civil servants have long experience and keep government records, so they advise ministers on the likely effects of policies and help draft policy proposals, in addition to implementing them.

whyNot.B: Passing bills is the work of the legislature.
whyNot.A: Hearing appeals is the work of the courts.
whyNot.D: Presidential elections are conducted by INEC.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Workers across the country stay away from work for three days after their union calls on them to press for a new minimum wage. Which pressure group method is this?
questions.explanation: A strike is when workers withdraw their labour to force employers or government to meet their demands. Labour unions such as the NLC use strikes to press for better wages.

whyNot.A: Lobbying is persuading officials privately.
whyNot.D: Litigation is going to court.
whyNot.C: Petition writing is sending formal written complaints or requests.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which of the following is a way in which pressure groups help democracy?
options: They conduct elections in place of INEC
They appoint ministers and permanent secretaries
They express the views of different groups to government and educate the public on issues
They take over government when the ruling party loses popularity
questions.explanation: Pressure groups give citizens a channel, apart from elections, to tell government what they want. They also enlighten the public on issues and act as a check on government, all of which strengthen democracy.

whyNot.D: Pressure groups do not seek to take over government.
whyNot.B: Appointments are made by the executive.
whyNot.A: Elections are conducted by electoral commissions.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: An organisation with a clear hierarchy, officials appointed on merit, and work governed by written rules is called a bureaucracy. Which scholar is best known for this model?
questions.explanation: The German sociologist Max Weber described the ideal bureaucracy: a hierarchy of offices, officials selected on merit and trained, fixed written rules, impersonal treatment and careful records. Modern civil services are built on this model.

whyNot.D: Montesquieu is known for separation of powers.
whyNot.A: Dicey is known for the rule of law.
whyNot.C: Lincoln is known for his definition of democracy.

questions.subject: civic-education
questions.stem: Which anti-corruption agency was established under the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act of 2000?
options: Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC)
questions.explanation: The ICPC was set up under the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000 to receive and investigate reports of corruption, especially in the public service, prosecute offenders and educate the public against corruption.

whyNot.B: The EFCC was created under a separate law to fight economic and financial crimes.
whyNot.D: The Code of Conduct Bureau is provided for in the Constitution and handles asset declarations by public officers.
whyNot.C: The PCC is the ombudsman for administrative injustice.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which of the following best describes entrepot trade?
options: Importing goods in order to re-export them to other countries
Selling goods produced at home to buyers in other countries
Buying and selling goods between two states of the same country
Buying goods from abroad for use within the home country
questions.explanation: Entrepot (re-export) trade is when a country imports goods, often stores or repacks them, and then exports them again to other countries. The goods are not meant for home consumption.

whyNot.D: That is simply import trade.
whyNot.B: That is export trade.
whyNot.C: Trade between states of one country is home (domestic) trade.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Commerce is made up of trade and aids to trade. Which of the following is NOT an aid to trade?
questions.explanation: Aids to trade are services that make buying and selling easier: banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, advertising and communication. Manufacturing is production of goods (secondary/industrial occupation), not an aid to trade.

whyNot.A: Banking helps trade by providing finance and means of payment.
whyNot.D: Insurance helps trade by covering traders against risks.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: In which type of retail outlet do customers pick goods from open shelves into baskets and pay for everything at a checkout point near the exit?
questions.explanation: A supermarket is a large self-service store: goods are displayed on open shelves, customers serve themselves and pay at checkout counters on their way out.

whyNot.C: In mail-order business, customers order from a catalogue and goods are sent to them; they never walk through a shop.
whyNot.B: A mobile shop is a vehicle that takes goods to customers; it has no checkout aisle.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A manufacturer is most likely to sell directly to final consumers, without wholesalers or retailers, when the goods are
options: cheap items that consumers buy daily in small quantities
needed by consumers scattered all over the country
produced by many small manufacturers in different towns
made to each customer's own specifications
questions.explanation: Goods made to order (for example custom furniture or specialised machines) need close contact between producer and buyer, so the producer deals with the consumer directly. Cheap everyday goods for scattered consumers are better sold through wholesalers and retailers.

whyNot.A: Cheap everyday goods bought in small quantities need retailers close to consumers.
whyNot.B: Scattered consumers are best reached through a chain of middlemen, not directly.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: In one year a country's visible exports were worth ₦850 billion, its visible imports ₦1,020 billion and its invisible exports ₦300 billion. What was its balance of trade?
questions.explanation: The balance of trade compares visible exports with visible imports only. ₦850 billion − ₦1,020 billion = −₦170 billion. A negative figure means imports exceed exports, so it is a deficit (unfavourable balance). Invisible items are left out.

whyNot.D: ₦130 billion comes from wrongly adding the invisible exports (850 + 300 − 1,020).
whyNot.B: The figure is right but imports are bigger than exports, so it is a deficit, not a surplus.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason why the wholesaler is often eliminated from the chain of distribution today?
options: Large-scale retailers buy in bulk directly from manufacturers
Small retailers need credit to stock their shops
Consumers live far away from the factories
Manufacturers prefer to deliver small quantities to many shops
questions.explanation: Supermarket chains, department stores and other large retailers have the money and storage space to buy in bulk, so they deal with manufacturers directly and keep the wholesaler's profit for themselves.

whyNot.B: Credit to small retailers is a service wholesalers provide, so it is a reason to keep them.
whyNot.D: Delivering small quantities to many shops is costly, which is exactly why manufacturers use wholesalers.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The Federal Government announces that a particular product may not be brought into Nigeria at all. This complete ban on importation is called
questions.explanation: An embargo is a total ban on the import (or export) of a good. A quota only limits the quantity, and a tariff is a tax on imports.

whyNot.B: A quota fixes a maximum quantity that may be imported; it does not ban the good completely.
whyNot.A: A tariff is a customs duty that makes imports dearer but still allows them in.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A retailer in Onitsha buys a radio for ₦24,000 and sells it for ₦30,000. What is her gross profit margin (profit as a percentage of the selling price)?
questions.explanation: Gross profit = ₦30,000 − ₦24,000 = ₦6,000. Margin = profit ÷ selling price × 100 = 6,000 ÷ 30,000 × 100 = 20%.

whyNot.A: 25% is the mark-up: profit as a percentage of cost (6,000 ÷ 24,000).
whyNot.D: 6 is the profit in thousands of naira, not a percentage.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A shop's opening stock was ₦40,000 and its closing stock was ₦60,000 at cost. Its cost of goods sold for the year was ₦300,000. What was its rate of turnover?
questions.explanation: Average stock = (opening stock + closing stock) ÷ 2 = (40,000 + 60,000) ÷ 2 = ₦50,000. Rate of turnover = cost of goods sold ÷ average stock = 300,000 ÷ 50,000 = 6 times.

whyNot.D: 5 times divides by the closing stock only.
whyNot.C: 7.5 times divides by the opening stock only.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Under which arrangement does ownership of goods pass to the buyer only after the last instalment has been paid?
questions.explanation: In hire purchase the buyer (hirer) takes possession of the goods at once but the seller remains the owner until the final instalment is paid. In a credit sale, ownership passes immediately even though payment is spread out.

whyNot.B: In a credit sale ownership passes to the buyer at once.
whyNot.C: With cash on delivery the buyer pays in full when the goods arrive, so there are no instalments.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which principle of insurance requires a person applying for insurance to disclose every material fact about the risk?
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) means both parties must be completely honest. The proposer must reveal every fact that could affect the insurer's decision or the premium; hiding one can make the policy void.

whyNot.B: Indemnity is about restoring the insured to his former position after a loss.
whyNot.C: Subrogation gives the insurer the insured's rights after a claim is paid.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which means of transport moves petroleum products continuously over long distances on land with very little labour?
questions.explanation: Pipelines carry liquids and gas such as crude oil, petrol and natural gas non-stop, are not affected by traffic, and need few workers once laid.

whyNot.C: Road tankers need drivers for every load and are affected by traffic and bad roads.
whyNot.B: Air transport is far too expensive for bulky liquids like petroleum.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Imported goods on which customs duty has not yet been paid are kept in a
questions.explanation: A bonded warehouse is approved by the Customs Service to hold imported goods before duty is paid. The importer pays duty only when goods are taken out, in instalments if he wishes.

whyNot.A: A public warehouse stores goods for anyone for a fee; it is not specially for duty-unpaid goods.
whyNot.B: A manufacturer's warehouse holds the firm's own raw materials and finished goods.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The principle of insurable interest means that the person taking out an insurance policy must
options: suffer a financial loss if the insured property is lost or damaged
disclose all material facts to the insurer
not make a profit from a loss
share any loss with other insurers of the same property
questions.explanation: Insurable interest means the insured must have a financial stake in the subject matter: he benefits from its safety and loses money if it is damaged. Without this, insurance would be mere gambling.

whyNot.B: That is the principle of utmost good faith.
whyNot.C: That is the principle of indemnity.
whyNot.D: That describes the principle of contribution.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: An insurance company paid Mr Eze the full value of his stolen car. Months later the police recovered the car. The insurer is now entitled to the car under the principle of
questions.explanation: Subrogation: once an insurer pays a claim in full, it takes over the insured's rights over the damaged or recovered property and against third parties. This stops Mr Eze from keeping both the money and the car.

whyNot.C: Contribution is about sharing a loss between two or more insurers.
whyNot.D: Proximate cause concerns whether the loss was directly caused by an insured risk.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A shop worth ₦2,000,000 is insured for only ₦1,500,000 under a policy with an average clause. A fire causes a loss of ₦400,000. How much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Under the average clause an under-insured person bears part of the loss. Claim = (sum insured ÷ value of property) × loss = (1,500,000 ÷ 2,000,000) × 400,000 = ¾ × 400,000 = ₦300,000.

whyNot.D: ₦400,000 would be paid only if the shop were fully insured.
whyNot.A: ₦1,500,000 is the sum insured, which is paid only for a total loss of a fully insured property.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria but NOT of commercial banks?
options: Acting as lender of last resort to other banks
Keeping customers' valuables in safe custody
questions.explanation: The Central Bank is the bankers' bank: when commercial banks run short of funds and cannot borrow elsewhere, the CBN lends to them as lender of last resort. Overdrafts, deposits and safe custody are services commercial banks give the public.

whyNot.A: Commercial banks grant overdrafts to their current account customers.
whyNot.B: Accepting deposits from the public is a main function of commercial banks.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A new clinic in Jos places a notice in a local newspaper giving its address, opening hours and the services it offers, without claiming to be better than anyone else. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Informative advertising simply gives facts — what is offered, where, when and at what price. It is common for new products and services so that people know they exist.

whyNot.A: Competitive advertising compares a product with rivals and claims it is better.
whyNot.B: Persuasive advertising uses appeals and slogans to make people want a product.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Life assurance is called a contract of assurance rather than insurance mainly because
options: the event covered is certain to happen and only its timing is uncertain
the person assured must disclose all material facts
the policy can be cancelled by the insurer at any time
the premium is paid every month instead of every year
questions.explanation: Death is certain; only when it will happen is uncertain. So a life policy (or an endowment policy maturing at a set date) will certainly pay out — it 'assures' a sum. Insurance covers events such as fire or theft that may never happen.

whyNot.B: Disclosure (utmost good faith) applies to both insurance and assurance, so it is not the difference.
whyNot.D: Premiums for many kinds of policy can be paid monthly; the frequency is not what makes it assurance.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which of the following is a major advantage of containerisation in transporting goods?
options: It removes the need for any insurance on the goods
It allows each item to be inspected easily during the journey
It makes it possible to carry goods without using ships or lorries
It reduces theft and damage because goods are sealed in standard boxes
questions.explanation: Containers are strong, standard-sized steel boxes that are sealed at the start of the journey and moved easily between ships, lorries and trains. Sealing reduces pilferage and damage, and standard sizes speed up loading.

whyNot.A: Goods in containers still face risks such as sinking or fire, so they are still insured.
whyNot.B: Sealed containers are not opened during the journey, so items cannot be easily inspected.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The liability of a sole trader for the debts of the business is
questions.explanation: A sole trader and the business are not separate in law. If the business cannot pay its debts, creditors may take the owner's private property, such as his house or car. This is unlimited liability.

whyNot.B: Liability limited to capital invested applies to shareholders of limited companies.
whyNot.A: A sole trader has no shareholders.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which document sets out the internal rules of a company, such as how directors are appointed and how meetings are conducted?
questions.explanation: The articles of association are the company's internal rules: appointment and powers of directors, conduct of meetings, voting rights and transfer of shares. The memorandum deals with the company's relationship with the outside world.

whyNot.D: The memorandum gives the company's name, objects, liability of members and share capital — its external constitution.
whyNot.A: A prospectus invites the public to buy a public company's shares.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which body registers companies and business names in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Under the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA), the Corporate Affairs Commission registers companies, business names and incorporated trustees and issues certificates of incorporation.

whyNot.D: SEC regulates the capital market; it does not register companies.
whyNot.C: NGX is the stock exchange where shares of listed companies are traded.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A partner who contributes capital and shares in the profits but takes no part in running the business is called a
questions.explanation: A sleeping (dormant) partner provides capital and takes a share of profit but does not take part in management. The business is run by the active partners.

whyNot.A: A nominal partner only lends his name and reputation; he usually contributes no capital and takes no profit.
whyNot.C: An active partner takes part in running the business.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Holders of which type of shares receive a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid anything?
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders are entitled to a fixed percentage dividend that must be paid before ordinary shareholders receive any dividend. In exchange they usually have little or no voting right.

whyNot.B: Ordinary shareholders are paid last and their dividend varies with profit.
whyNot.A: Deferred shares are paid only after both preference and ordinary shareholders.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A company has ₦500,000 of 8% preference shares and 200,000 ordinary shares. Profit available for dividend is ₦140,000, and it is all paid out. What dividend is paid on each ordinary share?
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders are paid first: 8% of ₦500,000 = ₦40,000. The rest, ₦140,000 − ₦40,000 = ₦100,000, goes to ordinary shareholders: ₦100,000 ÷ 200,000 shares = ₦0.50, which is 50 kobo per share.

whyNot.D: 70 kobo shares all ₦140,000 among ordinary shares, forgetting to pay preference shareholders first.
whyNot.C: 20 kobo shares only the preference dividend (₦40,000) among the 200,000 ordinary shares.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: An investor applies for shares in a new public offer, hoping to sell them at a quick profit as soon as trading in them begins. On the stock exchange, such an investor is called a
questions.explanation: A stag buys new issues of shares, not to keep them, but to sell them quickly at a premium once they start trading on the exchange.

whyNot.D: A bull buys existing shares expecting their prices to rise generally.
whyNot.B: A bear sells shares expecting prices to fall.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which body regulates the capital market, including the activities of stockbrokers and public offers of shares, in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Securities and Exchange Commission is the apex regulator of Nigeria's capital market. It registers securities and market operators such as brokers and approves public offers.

whyNot.A: The CBN regulates banks and monetary policy, not the capital market.
whyNot.D: NAICOM regulates insurance companies.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of a cooperative society?
options: Each member has one vote, no matter how many shares he holds
Only the founding members may vote at meetings
Votes are given in proportion to the number of shares held
Profits are shared only according to the capital each member contributed
questions.explanation: Cooperatives are run democratically: one member, one vote. Surplus is usually shared according to how much each member bought from or sold through the society (patronage), not according to capital.

whyNot.C: Voting according to shares held is a feature of limited companies.
whyNot.D: Cooperatives share surplus mainly by patronage, not by capital.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A public corporation differs from a public limited company in that a public corporation
options: can sue and be sued in its own name
is owned and financed by government
questions.explanation: A public corporation is set up by an Act of the legislature and owned and financed by government to provide essential services. A public limited company is owned by private shareholders who buy its shares.

whyNot.C: Both are separate legal entities, so this is not a difference.
whyNot.A: Both can sue and be sued in their own names.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A seller issues a credit note to a buyer
options: to increase the amount the buyer owes after an undercharge
to acknowledge that the buyer has paid
to reduce the amount the buyer owes, for example after goods are returned
to ask the buyer for a price quotation
questions.explanation: A credit note is sent by the seller to reduce the buyer's debt, for example when goods are returned, damaged, or the buyer was overcharged.

whyNot.A: That is the purpose of a debit note.
whyNot.B: A receipt acknowledges payment.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A cheque has two parallel lines drawn across its face. This means it
options: cannot be paid until a future date written on it
can only be paid into a bank account, not cashed over the counter
can be cashed over the counter by anyone who presents it
has been refused payment by the bank
questions.explanation: Two parallel lines make a crossed cheque. A crossed cheque must be paid into a bank account, which makes it safer: if stolen, the money can be traced to an account.

whyNot.C: That describes an open (uncrossed) cheque.
whyNot.A: That describes a post-dated cheque.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Goods with a list price of ₦80,000 are sold subject to 20% trade discount and 5% cash discount for payment within 7 days. How much does the buyer pay if he pays within 7 days?
questions.explanation: Trade discount comes off first: 20% of ₦80,000 = ₦16,000, so the invoice price is ₦64,000. Cash discount is then taken on the invoice price: 5% of ₦64,000 = ₦3,200. Amount paid = ₦64,000 − ₦3,200 = ₦60,800.

whyNot.A: ₦60,000 adds the two discounts (25%) and takes them off the list price; cash discount is calculated on the net price.
whyNot.C: ₦64,000 is the invoice price after trade discount only.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which document is a receipt for goods shipped, evidence of the contract of carriage by sea and a document of title to the goods?
questions.explanation: The bill of lading is signed by the shipowner or his agent. It acknowledges receipt of the goods, contains the terms of carriage, and whoever holds it can claim the goods at the port of arrival — so it is a document of title.

whyNot.D: A consular invoice is certified by the importing country's consul to confirm value for customs purposes.
whyNot.C: A certificate of origin states where the goods were made.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: An exporter in Ghana is reluctant to ship goods to a new buyer in Kano. Which arrangement best assures him of payment?
options: A credit note issued by the buyer
A bill of sight lodged with customs
A letter of credit opened by the buyer's bank
A pro forma invoice sent by the exporter
questions.explanation: Under a letter of credit, the importer's bank undertakes to pay the exporter once he presents the agreed shipping documents (such as the bill of lading). The exporter relies on the bank's promise, not just the buyer's.

whyNot.D: A pro forma invoice only states what the goods will cost; it does not guarantee payment.
whyNot.B: A bill of sight is used when an importer cannot fully describe goods for customs; it has nothing to do with payment.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A trader in Aba wants a new customer to pay before goods are sent. Which document should she send to show what the goods will cost?
questions.explanation: A pro forma invoice looks like an ordinary invoice but is sent before the goods are supplied. It is used to request payment in advance, to give a formal quotation, or for goods sent on approval.

whyNot.C: A credit note reduces an amount already owed.
whyNot.A: A statement of account summarises past transactions with an existing customer.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.context: Order from Bisi Stores, Ibadan: 40 cartons of biscuits at ₦2,500 per carton. Terms: 10% trade discount on the goods; carriage of ₦5,000 is charged in full with no discount.
questions.stem: What is the total amount on the invoice?
questions.explanation: Goods: 40 × ₦2,500 = ₦100,000. Less 10% trade discount (₦10,000) = ₦90,000. Add carriage of ₦5,000 (not discounted) = ₦95,000.

whyNot.A: ₦94,500 wrongly takes the discount off the carriage as well: (100,000 + 5,000) × 0.9.
whyNot.D: ₦105,000 ignores the trade discount.
whyNot.B: ₦90,000 leaves out the carriage charge.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Mrs Okafor instructs her bank to pay a fixed sum of ₦25,000 from her account to her landlord on the first day of every month. This is a
questions.explanation: A standing order is an instruction from a customer to her bank to pay a fixed amount to a named person at regular intervals until cancelled.

whyNot.D: In a direct debit the payee claims the money, and the amount may vary each time.
whyNot.A: A bank draft is a single cheque drawn by a bank on itself for one payment.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A cheque dated 10 January 2025 was presented for payment on 15 September 2025. The bank refused to pay it only because of the time that had passed since its date. The cheque was
questions.explanation: A cheque that is presented too long after its date — in Nigerian banking practice, more than six months — becomes stale, and the bank will not pay it. Here about eight months had passed. The drawer can issue a fresh cheque.

whyNot.B: A post-dated cheque bears a future date; this one bears a past date.
whyNot.C: A countermanded cheque is one the drawer has stopped; here the refusal was only due to time.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: On an invoice, the abbreviation 'E & OE' stands for
questions.explanation: 'E & OE' means errors and omissions excepted. It reserves the seller's right to correct any mistake or omission on the invoice later, for example with a debit or credit note.

whyNot.A: It has nothing to do with exports or exemptions.
whyNot.D: Excise duty is a tax and is not what the abbreviation means.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which agency registers and controls the quality of food, drugs, cosmetics and packaged water in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) registers and regulates food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals and packaged water. Registered products carry a NAFDAC number.

whyNot.D: SON sets and enforces standards for manufactured products generally.
whyNot.A: The NCC regulates telecommunications.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The Latin expression 'caveat emptor' means
options: goods must be paid for in cash
questions.explanation: Caveat emptor means 'let the buyer beware': the buyer should examine goods carefully before buying, because the seller may not be responsible for defects. Consumer protection laws reduce the harshness of this rule.

whyNot.C: This is close to the opposite of caveat emptor.
whyNot.B: 'The customer is king' is a business slogan, not the meaning of caveat emptor.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which body was established by the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018 to protect consumers and promote fair competition in Nigeria?
options: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC)
questions.explanation: The FCCPA 2018 created the FCCPC, which replaced the former Consumer Protection Council. It handles consumer complaints, fights unfair trade practices and regulates competition and mergers.

whyNot.A: SON was not created by that Act; it deals with product standards.
whyNot.B: NDIC insures bank deposits.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) protects consumers mainly by
options: registering drugs and packaged food before they are sold
setting quality standards for products and checking that goods meet them
regulating the charges of telephone companies
questions.explanation: SON prepares the Nigerian Industrial Standards and checks that locally made and imported products meet them, for example through its MANCAP and SONCAP programmes. This keeps substandard goods out of the market.

whyNot.A: Registering drugs and packaged food is NAFDAC's work.
whyNot.C: Telecom charges are regulated by the Nigerian Communications Commission.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Chidi bought a new blender that stopped working on the first day. The shop repaired it free of charge. Which consumer right did this satisfy?
questions.explanation: The right to redress is the right to a fair settlement of genuine complaints — repair, replacement, refund or compensation — when goods or services are faulty.

whyNot.D: The right to choose is about having a variety of goods at competitive prices.
whyNot.A: The right to be informed is about getting accurate facts such as price, ingredients and directions for use.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Under the Sale of Goods law, when goods are sold by description, the seller is taken to promise that
options: the goods will be delivered free of charge
the goods will correspond with the description
the buyer may return them for any reason
the price will not change for a year
questions.explanation: One of the implied conditions in the Sale of Goods Act is that goods sold by description must match that description. If a buyer orders '100% cotton' shirts and receives polyester ones, the seller is in breach and the buyer may reject them.

whyNot.C: The law protects buyers against faulty or wrongly described goods, not returns for any reason at all.
whyNot.A: Delivery charges depend on the agreement between buyer and seller, not an implied term.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A student in Ilorin orders a phone on an online store run by an electronics company. This type of e-commerce is
questions.explanation: The seller is a business and the buyer is a final consumer buying for personal use, so this is business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce.

whyNot.A: B2B is when one firm sells to another firm, e.g. a manufacturer to a retailer.
whyNot.C: C2C is when individuals sell to one another, e.g. used items on an online marketplace.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of e-commerce to a small business?
options: It never needs to deliver goods to customers
It can reach customers in many states without opening physical shops
It removes all risk of fraud in payments
It no longer needs to keep any records
questions.explanation: Selling online lets even a small business display goods to buyers across Nigeria and beyond, 24 hours a day, without the cost of renting shops in many places.

whyNot.A: Goods bought online still have to be delivered.
whyNot.C: Online payment fraud remains a real risk that must be guarded against.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A law requires that packaged goods show the price, ingredients, net weight and expiry date. This protects consumers mainly through
questions.explanation: Labelling laws make sure consumers are informed: they can see what is in a product, how much they are getting and whether it is still safe to use.

whyNot.C: Price control fixes maximum prices; it does not require information on packages.
whyNot.A: Rationing limits how much each consumer may buy.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A bag of rice labelled 50 kg is sold for ₦45,000, but when weighed it contains only 46 kg. At the price per kilogram implied by the label, how much has the buyer been cheated?
questions.explanation: Price per kg implied by the label = ₦45,000 ÷ 50 = ₦900. Missing rice = 50 − 46 = 4 kg. Loss = 4 × ₦900 = ₦3,600. Weights and measures laws exist to stop such short-weighting.

whyNot.B: ₦4,000 assumes ₦1,000 per kg instead of working out the price per kg.
whyNot.A: ₦900 is the value of only 1 kg.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Home trade is made up of
questions.explanation: Home (domestic) trade is buying and selling within one country. It is divided into wholesale trade (selling in bulk to retailers) and retail trade (selling in small quantities to consumers).

whyNot.C: Import and export trade are the two parts of foreign trade.
whyNot.A: Entrepot and export trade both involve other countries.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: What is the main function of a retailer?
options: Turning raw materials into finished goods
Buying in bulk from manufacturers to sell to other traders
Shipping goods to buyers in other countries
Selling goods to final consumers in small quantities
questions.explanation: The retailer is the last link in the chain of distribution. He buys from wholesalers or manufacturers and sells to final consumers in the small quantities they need.

whyNot.B: That is the work of the wholesaler.
whyNot.A: That is manufacturing (production), not trade.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The major problem of trade by barter is the
options: lack of double coincidence of wants
questions.explanation: In barter, goods are exchanged directly for goods. A trade happens only if each person wants what the other has — a double coincidence of wants — which is hard to find. Money solved this problem.

whyNot.A: Middlemen are a feature of a money economy, not the main problem of barter.
whyNot.C: There are no banks in a pure barter system.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A large shop in Lagos sells clothing, furniture, electronics and cosmetics in separate sections, all under one roof and one management. This is a
questions.explanation: A department store is a large shop divided into departments, each selling a different class of goods, all under one roof and one central management.

whyNot.D: A chain (multiple) store has many branches in different places, usually selling the same range of goods.
whyNot.C: A mail-order house sells through catalogues and delivers by post or courier.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A retail business has many branches in different towns, all looking alike, selling the same type of goods at the same prices and controlled from a head office. It is a
questions.explanation: Chain stores (multiple shops) have identical branches in many towns, sell standardised goods at uniform prices and are centrally controlled by a head office, which buys in bulk for all branches.

whyNot.C: A department store is one large building with many departments, not many branches.
whyNot.A: A unit shop is a single independent shop.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Nigeria earns money from foreign tourists who visit the Obudu Mountain Resort. For Nigeria, this is
questions.explanation: Tourism is a service, so it is invisible. Because foreigners pay money to Nigeria for the service, it is an export. Hence spending by foreign tourists in Nigeria is an invisible export.

whyNot.B: Visible exports are physical goods such as crude oil or cocoa.
whyNot.A: It would be an invisible import if Nigerians spent money on holidays abroad.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: In a year a country recorded: visible exports ₦600 billion, visible imports ₦450 billion, invisible exports ₦120 billion and invisible imports ₦310 billion. What was its balance of payments on current account?
questions.explanation: Current account = (visible exports + invisible exports) − (visible imports + invisible imports) = (600 + 120) − (450 + 310) = 720 − 760 = −₦40 billion, a deficit.

whyNot.B: ₦150 billion surplus is only the balance of trade (visibles: 600 − 450).
whyNot.D: ₦190 billion deficit is only the invisible balance (120 − 310).
whyNot.C: The size is right but outgoings exceed receipts, so it is a deficit.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The main reason countries engage in international trade is that
options: it helps traders avoid paying customs duties
differences in natural resources and climate make each country better at producing some goods
it reduces the number of banks needed in a country
every country can produce all the goods it needs
questions.explanation: Resources, climate and skills are unevenly spread. Countries specialise in what they produce best and trade to get what they cannot produce cheaply, e.g. Nigeria exports crude oil and imports machinery.

whyNot.D: If every country could produce everything cheaply, there would be little need for trade.
whyNot.A: International trade usually attracts customs duties rather than avoiding them.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A trader adds a mark-up of 25% to the cost of her goods to get the selling price. What is her profit as a percentage of the selling price?
questions.explanation: Take cost as ₦100. Mark-up of 25% gives profit ₦25 and selling price ₦125. Margin = 25 ÷ 125 × 100 = 20%.

whyNot.B: 25% is the mark-up on cost, not the margin on selling price.
whyNot.C: 33⅓% is the mark-up that gives a 25% margin, which is the reverse relationship.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which of the following is a service the wholesaler renders to the manufacturer?
options: Selling goods in small quantities to final consumers
Allowing consumers to pay for goods in instalments
Giving consumers after-sales service at their homes
Buying in large quantities and relieving him of storage
questions.explanation: By buying in bulk, the wholesaler takes goods off the manufacturer's hands soon after production. This frees the manufacturer's storage space, gives him money quickly and lets him concentrate on production.

whyNot.A: Selling in small quantities to consumers is the retailer's job.
whyNot.B: Instalment selling to consumers is done by retailers, not a service to the manufacturer.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The insurance principle which states that the insured should be restored to the same financial position as before the loss, but must not profit from it, is
questions.explanation: Indemnity means exact compensation: the insurer pays enough to put the insured back where he was before the loss, no more. This removes any temptation to cause a loss deliberately.

whyNot.A: Subrogation follows from indemnity but is about the insurer taking over the insured's rights.
whyNot.C: Insurable interest is about having a financial stake in what is insured.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The document issued by an insurer that contains all the terms and conditions of the insurance contract is the
questions.explanation: The policy is the formal written contract of insurance. It states the risks covered, the sum insured, the premium, the period and the conditions.

whyNot.A: The proposal form is filled in by the person seeking insurance before cover is given.
whyNot.C: A cover note is temporary proof of cover issued while the policy is being prepared.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Goods worth ₦4,000,000 are insured at a premium rate of ₦2.50 per ₦100. What is the premium?

whyNot.D: ₦10,000 treats the rate as ₦2.50 per ₦1,000.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Mr Danjuma insured the same warehouse with Insurer X for ₦3,000,000 and with Insurer Y for ₦1,000,000. A fire causes a loss of ₦800,000. Under the principle of contribution, how much does Insurer X pay?
questions.explanation: Under contribution, each insurer pays in proportion to the sum it insured. Total sum insured = ₦4,000,000. X's share = 3,000,000 ÷ 4,000,000 = ¾. X pays ¾ × ₦800,000 = ₦600,000 (and Y pays ₦200,000).

whyNot.B: ₦400,000 splits the loss equally, ignoring the different sums insured.
whyNot.C: ₦800,000 would let Mr Danjuma collect more than his loss if Y also paid.
whyNot.A: ₦200,000 is Insurer Y's share.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: An insurer will pay a claim only if the loss was directly caused by a risk covered in the policy. This is the principle of
questions.explanation: Proximate cause means the insurer looks for the main, direct cause of the loss. If that cause is an insured risk, the claim is paid; if it is an excluded risk, it is not.

whyNot.A: Contribution is about sharing a loss among insurers.
whyNot.B: Indemnity is about how much is paid, not what caused the loss.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Air transport is most suitable for carrying
options: urgently needed, light and high-value goods
bulky goods such as cement and iron rods
crude oil from oil fields to refineries
cheap goods over short distances within a town
questions.explanation: Air is the fastest but most expensive means of transport, and aircraft carry limited weight. It suits urgent, light, valuable or perishable goods such as medicines, documents, jewellery and fresh flowers.

whyNot.B: Bulky, heavy goods are cheaper to move by rail or water.
whyNot.C: Crude oil is moved by pipelines or tankers.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A bank overdraft allows a customer to
options: withdraw more money than is in his current account, up to an agreed limit
transfer a fixed sum to another person every month
keep valuable documents in the bank's strong room
receive interest on money saved for a fixed period
questions.explanation: An overdraft is a short-term facility on a current account: the bank allows the customer to draw beyond his balance up to a limit, and charges interest only on the amount overdrawn.

whyNot.D: That describes a fixed (time) deposit account.
whyNot.B: That describes a standing order.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Farmers store their maize after harvest and sell it later in the year when it is scarce. Warehousing here mainly creates
questions.explanation: Warehousing keeps goods until they are needed, bridging the gap between when goods are produced and when they are consumed. This adds time utility and helps steady prices.

whyNot.C: Place utility is created mainly by transport, which moves goods to where they are needed.
whyNot.D: Form utility is created by changing the shape of goods, as in manufacturing.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: An insurance company that has accepted a very large risk passes part of it to another insurance company. This practice is called
questions.explanation: Reinsurance is insurance for insurers: the first insurer transfers part of a large risk (and part of the premium) to a reinsurer, so that one big loss cannot ruin it.

whyNot.B: Double insurance is when the insured himself insures the same risk with two insurers.
whyNot.D: Assignment is the transfer of a policy's benefits from one person to another.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which advertising medium is most likely to reach farmers who cannot read in villages across several states?
questions.explanation: Radio reaches large numbers of people in rural areas cheaply, broadcasts in local languages and does not require the listener to read.

whyNot.C: Newspapers need readers who can read and are less available in villages.
whyNot.D: Direct mail is printed and posted, so it also needs reading and good postal addresses.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The owners of a limited liability company are its
questions.explanation: A company is owned by its members, the shareholders, who buy its shares. The directors are elected by shareholders to manage it.

whyNot.A: Directors manage the company but may own no shares at all.
whyNot.D: Debenture holders are creditors who have lent money to the company.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The written agreement that sets out how partners will share profits, contribute capital and run their business is the
questions.explanation: The partnership deed (deed of partnership) contains the partners' agreement on capital, profit sharing, interest on capital, drawings, duties and how disputes are settled.

whyNot.C: Articles of association are a company's internal rules.
whyNot.B: A prospectus invites the public to buy a public company's shares.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which business unit is a separate legal entity with limited liability but may NOT invite the general public to buy its shares?
questions.explanation: A private limited company (Ltd) has limited liability and its own legal personality, but it is not allowed to offer its shares to the public. A public limited company (Plc) can.

whyNot.D: A public limited company may invite the public to subscribe for its shares.
whyNot.B: An ordinary partnership is not a separate legal entity and has unlimited liability.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Holders of debentures in a company are
options: managers elected at the annual general meeting
owners who receive a share of the profits
creditors who receive a fixed rate of interest
workers who are paid by results
questions.explanation: A debenture is a loan to the company. Debenture holders are creditors, not owners: they receive a fixed interest whether or not a profit is made, and are repaid before shareholders if the company is wound up.

whyNot.B: Owners who share profits are shareholders.
whyNot.A: Directors are elected at the AGM to manage the company.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Ade and Bola are partners with capitals of ₦600,000 and ₦400,000. Their deed gives 5% interest on capital and shares the rest of the profit equally. If profit for the year is ₦200,000, what is Ade's total share?

whyNot.B: ₦120,000 shares the whole profit in the capital ratio 3 : 2.
whyNot.D: ₦100,000 shares the whole profit equally and forgets interest on capital.
whyNot.C: ₦75,000 is only his half of the remaining profit.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Cocoa farmers in Ondo State pool their produce so that they can grade it and sell it together at better prices. They have formed a
questions.explanation: Producer cooperatives are formed by producers such as farmers to process, grade and market their produce jointly, getting better prices and avoiding exploitation by middlemen.

whyNot.D: A consumer cooperative is formed by consumers to buy goods cheaply for their members.
whyNot.C: A thrift and credit cooperative collects members' savings and gives them loans.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: On the stock exchange, an investor who sells shares because he expects their prices to fall, hoping to buy them back later more cheaply, is called a
questions.explanation: A bear is a pessimistic speculator: he sells now expecting prices to fall, so that he can buy later at a lower price and gain the difference.

whyNot.D: A bull buys expecting prices to rise.
whyNot.A: A stag buys new issues to resell quickly at a profit.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the stock exchange?
options: Registering new companies and business names
Providing a market for buying and selling existing shares
Insuring the deposits of bank customers
questions.explanation: The stock exchange (in Nigeria, the Nigerian Exchange, NGX) is a market where existing securities of listed companies and government stocks are bought and sold, making it easy for investors to turn shares into cash.

whyNot.A: Registering companies is the work of the Corporate Affairs Commission.
whyNot.B: The Central Bank of Nigeria issues the currency.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The sale of government-owned shares in public enterprises to private individuals and firms is called
questions.explanation: Privatisation transfers ownership of public enterprises, wholly or partly, from government to private investors, usually by selling shares.

whyNot.A: Nationalisation is the opposite: government takes over private businesses.
whyNot.D: Commercialisation keeps government ownership but requires the enterprise to run profitably without subsidies.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Funke owns 6,000 shares in a company that makes a 1-for-3 rights issue at ₦2 per share. How much must she pay to take up all her rights?
questions.explanation: A 1-for-3 rights issue offers one new share for every three held. New shares = 6,000 ÷ 3 = 2,000. Cost = 2,000 × ₦2 = ₦4,000.

whyNot.B: ₦12,000 prices all 6,000 existing shares at ₦2 instead of the new shares only.
whyNot.C: 2,000 is the number of new shares, not their cost in naira.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Okon was undercharged by ₦4,000 on an invoice. Which document should the seller send to correct this?
questions.explanation: A debit note is issued by the seller to increase the amount the buyer owes, for example after an undercharge on an invoice.

whyNot.C: A credit note reduces the amount owed, so it is used for overcharges or returns.
whyNot.B: A delivery note accompanies goods so the buyer can check them; it does not change amounts owed.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The first document usually sent by a prospective buyer to a seller is a
questions.explanation: A buyer begins by sending a letter of enquiry asking about prices, terms, quality and delivery. The seller replies with a quotation, catalogue or price list.

whyNot.B: A quotation is the seller's reply to the enquiry.
whyNot.C: An invoice is sent by the seller after goods are ordered or supplied.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: The main purpose of a cash discount is to
options: allow retailers to make a profit on the list price
reward buyers for ordering in large quantities
reduce the price of damaged goods
questions.explanation: Cash discount is a reduction offered for paying within a stated period, e.g. '2½% within 14 days'. It speeds up payment and reduces bad debts.

whyNot.A: Trade discount is what lets retailers resell at the list price and make a profit.
whyNot.C: A reward for buying in bulk is a quantity discount.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A seller sends a customer a document at the end of the month showing the balance brought forward, invoices, credit notes, payments received and the amount now owing. This document is a
questions.explanation: A statement of account summarises all transactions with a customer during a period and shows the balance due. It reminds the customer to pay and lets both sides check their records.

whyNot.A: A pro forma invoice is sent before goods are supplied.
whyNot.D: A consignment note goes with goods sent by a carrier.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Goods listed at ₦150,000 are sold with 10% trade discount and 2½% cash discount for payment within 14 days. How much does the buyer pay if he pays within 14 days?

whyNot.D: ₦131,250 adds the two rates (12½%) and takes them off the list price.
whyNot.A: ₦135,000 is the amount after trade discount only.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: In a bill of exchange, the person to whom the bill is addressed and who is required to pay it is the
questions.explanation: The drawer writes the bill and orders payment; the drawee is the person ordered to pay, who signs ('accepts') it; the payee receives the money.

whyNot.B: The drawer is the person who writes the bill, usually the creditor.
whyNot.C: The payee is the person who receives payment.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which document in foreign trade states the country in which the goods were produced, often so that they can enjoy lower import duty?
questions.explanation: A certificate of origin shows where goods were made. Customs use it to apply the right duty, e.g. lower duties on goods from member states of a trade agreement such as ECOWAS.

whyNot.A: A bill of lading is the shipping receipt and document of title.
whyNot.D: A mate's receipt is given by the ship's officer when goods are loaded on board.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: An importer sends an order to a commission agent abroad, naming the particular manufacturer from whom the goods must be bought. This order is
questions.explanation: An indent is an order sent to an agent abroad. A closed (specific) indent names the manufacturer or brand; an open indent leaves the agent free to buy from any supplier.

whyNot.B: An open indent leaves the choice of supplier to the agent.
whyNot.C: A pro forma invoice is sent by a seller before supplying goods.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which payment card takes money directly from the cardholder's own bank account at the time of purchase?
questions.explanation: A debit card (used at ATMs, POS terminals and online) deducts payment straight from the holder's account, so it can only spend money that is there.

whyNot.D: A credit card uses money lent by the card issuer, which the holder repays later.
whyNot.B: A loyalty card records points for rewards; it does not make payments from an account.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Goods are quoted at $10,000 FOB. Freight to Lagos is $1,200 and insurance is $300. What is the CIF Lagos price?
questions.explanation: FOB (free on board) covers the goods until they are loaded on the ship. CIF (cost, insurance and freight) adds the insurance and freight to the destination: 10,000 + 1,200 + 300 = $11,500.

whyNot.D: $11,200 leaves out insurance (it is C & F, not CIF).
whyNot.B: $10,300 leaves out freight.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Which agency operates the MANCAP certification to show that locally manufactured products meet the Nigerian Industrial Standards?
questions.explanation: MANCAP (Mandatory Conformity Assessment Programme) is run by SON for products made in Nigeria; imported products are checked under SONCAP. Both aim to keep substandard goods off the market.

whyNot.D: NAFDAC registers food, drugs and cosmetics, giving them NAFDAC numbers, not MANCAP certificates.
whyNot.A: The FCCPC handles consumer complaints and competition, not product certification.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: In commerce, a consumer is a person who
options: produces goods for sale to others
buys goods in bulk in order to resell them
buys or uses goods and services for final use
advertises goods on behalf of a manufacturer
questions.explanation: A consumer is the final user of goods and services, buying for personal or household use rather than for resale or production.

whyNot.B: Buying to resell describes a wholesaler or retailer.
whyNot.A: That describes a producer or manufacturer.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Before buying a tin of tomato paste, what should a careful consumer check to make sure it is safe and approved?
options: How many other customers are in the shop
The distance of the shop from her house
Its expiry date and NAFDAC registration number
questions.explanation: An expired product may be harmful, and a NAFDAC number shows the product has been registered after checks on its safety and quality. Both should be on the label.

whyNot.A: Label colour says nothing about safety.
whyNot.C: The shop's location has nothing to do with the product's safety.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: When one firm controls a whole market and blocks other firms from entering it, which consumer right is most directly threatened?
questions.explanation: The right to choose means having a variety of goods at competitive prices. A monopoly that shuts out rivals removes alternatives and can raise prices. The FCCPC enforces competition law to prevent this.

whyNot.D: The right to safety concerns protection from dangerous goods.
whyNot.A: The right to redress is about compensation for faulty goods or services.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A subscriber complains that her mobile network keeps deducting airtime for services she never requested. Which regulator protects consumers in such telecom matters?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Communications Commission regulates telecommunications in Nigeria, including how operators treat subscribers, and receives complaints such as unauthorised deductions from airtime.

whyNot.A: NAFDAC deals with food, drugs and cosmetics.
whyNot.B: CAC registers companies; it does not handle consumer complaints.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: An online store sells a phone for ₦120,000 and charges ₦3,500 for delivery. It gives 10% discount on the phone price only (not on delivery) for paying online. What does a customer who pays online pay in total?
questions.explanation: Discount on the phone = 10% × ₦120,000 = ₦12,000, so the phone costs ₦108,000. Add delivery of ₦3,500 (no discount): ₦108,000 + ₦3,500 = ₦111,500.

whyNot.C: ₦111,150 wrongly applies the discount to delivery too: (120,000 + 3,500) × 0.9.
whyNot.B: ₦108,000 leaves out the delivery charge.
whyNot.D: ₦123,500 ignores the discount.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: Amaka sells her used textbooks to another student through an online marketplace. This type of e-commerce is
questions.explanation: Both the seller and the buyer are private individuals, so this is consumer-to-consumer (C2C) e-commerce. The marketplace only connects them.

whyNot.A: B2C is a business selling to individual consumers.
whyNot.D: B2B is one business selling to another.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: How does the 'pay on delivery' option offered by many online stores protect the buyer?
options: It allows her to avoid paying for the goods
It makes delivery faster than other options
She does not pay until she has received the goods
It guarantees the goods will never be faulty
questions.explanation: With pay on delivery, the buyer pays only when the goods reach her, so she cannot lose money to a seller who never sends the goods, and she can check the parcel first.

whyNot.D: Paying on delivery does not stop goods from being faulty; it only changes when payment is made.
whyNot.A: The buyer still pays; only the timing changes.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: When paying online with her card, Ngozi must enter a one-time password (OTP) sent to her phone. The main purpose of this is to
options: give the seller her bank account number
confirm that the real account holder is approving the payment
allow the seller to charge her again later without asking
reduce the price of the goods bought
questions.explanation: An OTP is a short code sent to the account holder's registered phone and valid only once. Entering it proves the payment is being made by the account owner, which protects against card fraud. It should never be shared with anyone.

whyNot.A: The OTP does not reveal account details to the seller.
whyNot.C: Each OTP works once, so it cannot be used for later charges.

questions.subject: commerce
questions.stem: A group of residents in Enugu forms an association that tests products, publishes its findings and petitions government about bad goods. Consumers are here being protected through
questions.explanation: Consumer associations are voluntary groups formed by consumers themselves to educate members, test products, publicise bad practices and press government and producers for better treatment.

whyNot.A: Legislation is made by government, not by a residents' group.
whyNot.D: Trade associations are formed by producers or sellers, not consumers.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Chiamaka's boutique has total assets of ₦850,000 and total liabilities of ₦230,000. What is her capital?
questions.explanation: The accounting equation is Assets = Capital + Liabilities, so Capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₦850,000 − ₦230,000 = ₦620,000.

whyNot.A: ₦1,080,000 adds liabilities to assets instead of subtracting them.
whyNot.B: ₦850,000 is total assets; part of the assets is financed by liabilities, not by the owner.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Mr Okafor pays his children's school fees from his own pocket, and his shop's records do not show this payment. Which accounting concept is being followed?
questions.explanation: The business entity concept treats the business as separate from its owner. Only the business's own transactions are recorded in its books, so the owner's private payments are left out.

whyNot.D: Going concern assumes the business will continue operating; it says nothing about separating private affairs.
whyNot.B: Consistency is about using the same methods from year to year.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Closing inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Which accounting concept does this rule mainly apply?
questions.explanation: Prudence says losses should be provided for as soon as they are foreseen, but gains should not be anticipated. Valuing inventory at the lower figure avoids overstating assets and profit.

whyNot.B: Money measurement only says that items must be expressible in money to be recorded.
whyNot.D: Duality is the idea that every transaction has two equal effects (debit and credit).

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Non-current assets are shown in the statement of financial position at cost less depreciation rather than at what they would fetch if sold off quickly. Which concept justifies this?
questions.explanation: The going concern concept assumes the business will continue for the foreseeable future. Its assets will be used, not sold off, so forced-sale values are not relevant and cost less depreciation is used.

whyNot.C: Materiality is about whether an item is significant enough to be treated separately.
whyNot.B: Realisation concerns when revenue is recognised, not how assets are valued.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: December's electricity bill of a business with a 31 December year end is paid in January of the following year, but it is charged as an expense of the year just ended. Which concept is applied?
questions.explanation: Under the accruals (matching) concept, expenses are recognised in the period in which they are incurred, not the period in which cash is paid. December's electricity belongs to the year just ended.

whyNot.B: Consistency means using the same accounting methods each year.
whyNot.A: Historical cost concerns recording assets at their original cost.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A trader buys goods on credit for ₦40,000. What is the effect of this transaction on the accounting equation?
questions.explanation: The trader now has more inventory (an asset up by ₦40,000) and owes the supplier ₦40,000 (a liability up by ₦40,000). Both sides of the equation rise by the same amount.
