whyNot.C: Capital rises only when the owner invests or the business makes a profit; buying on credit creates a debt.
whyNot.A: Assets and liabilities fall together when a debt is paid off, not when goods are bought on credit.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: At the start of the year Bisi's capital was ₦500,000. During the year she made a net profit of ₦120,000, brought in additional capital of ₦30,000 and took drawings of ₦45,000. What was her capital at the end of the year?
questions.explanation: Closing capital = opening capital + additional capital + net profit − drawings = ₦500,000 + ₦30,000 + ₦120,000 − ₦45,000 = ₦605,000.

whyNot.A: ₦650,000 forgets to deduct the drawings of ₦45,000.
whyNot.D: ₦695,000 adds drawings instead of subtracting them.
whyNot.B: ₦575,000 leaves out the additional capital and deducts drawings: ₦500,000 + ₦120,000 − ₦45,000.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A company has always depreciated its vehicles by the reducing balance method and continues to do so every year so that its results can be compared. Which concept is being followed?
questions.explanation: The consistency concept requires a business to keep using the same accounting methods from one period to the next, so that results of different years can be compared fairly.

whyNot.C: Prudence is about not overstating assets and profits.
whyNot.D: Duality is the two-sided (debit and credit) effect of each transaction.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A business buys a stapler for ₦3,500 and treats it as an expense, even though it will last for several years. Which concept allows this?
questions.explanation: The materiality concept allows items too small to affect users' decisions to be treated in the simplest way. Spreading ₦3,500 over several years would cost more effort than it is worth, so it is expensed at once.

whyNot.A: Realisation concerns when revenue is earned.
whyNot.D: Historical cost would record the stapler at ₦3,500 but does not explain why it is not treated as a non-current asset.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Emeka does not keep full double-entry records. His net assets were ₦1,200,000 at the start of the year and ₦1,450,000 at the end. During the year he took drawings of ₦180,000 and introduced extra capital of ₦100,000. What was his net profit for the year?
questions.explanation: Net assets equal capital. Increase in capital = ₦1,450,000 − ₦1,200,000 = ₦250,000. Profit = increase + drawings − capital introduced = ₦250,000 + ₦180,000 − ₦100,000 = ₦330,000.

whyNot.A: ₦250,000 is only the increase in net assets; it ignores drawings and the new capital.
whyNot.D: ₦530,000 adds the capital introduced instead of subtracting it.
whyNot.C: ₦170,000 subtracts drawings instead of adding them back.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: In which book of original entry is a credit purchase of goods for resale first recorded?
questions.explanation: Credit purchases of goods meant for resale are first entered in the purchases journal (purchases day book) from the suppliers' invoices, then posted to the ledger.

whyNot.D: The cash book records cash and bank transactions, and a credit purchase involves no cash at that time.
whyNot.B: The journal proper is used for unusual items such as credit purchases of non-current assets, not goods for resale.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A customer who bought goods on credit returns some of them because they are damaged. In which book is this first recorded?
questions.explanation: Goods returned by customers come back into the business, so they are returns inwards (sales returns). They are first recorded in the returns inwards journal from the credit notes issued.

whyNot.B: The returns outwards journal records goods the business sends back to its suppliers.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: In a three-column cash book, where is discount received recorded?
options: In the discount column on the debit side
In the bank column on the debit side
In the discount column on the credit side
In the cash column on the credit side
questions.explanation: Discount received is earned when the business pays a supplier, and payments are on the credit side. So it goes in the discount column on the credit side, beside the payment. The column total is then credited to discount received account.

whyNot.A: The debit-side discount column is for discount allowed to customers who pay the business.
whyNot.D: Discount is not cash; it is a memorandum column, not part of the cash balance.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Funmi keeps a petty cash book on the imprest system with a float of ₦40,000. During the week she spends ₦8,500 on transport, ₦6,200 on stationery, ₦3,750 on postage and ₦4,100 on cleaning. How much must the main cashier give her to restore the imprest?
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system the cashier reimburses exactly what was spent. Total spent = ₦8,500 + ₦6,200 + ₦3,750 + ₦4,100 = ₦22,550, which brings the float back to ₦40,000.

whyNot.A: ₦17,450 is the cash left in the petty cash box (₦40,000 − ₦22,550), not the amount to reimburse.
whyNot.C: ₦40,000 is the whole float; only the amount spent needs to be replaced.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A trader's cash account had an opening balance of ₦85,000. During the week he received ₦140,000 from cash sales and ₦45,000 from a debtor. He paid wages of ₦32,000, cash purchases of ₦78,000 and rent of ₦25,000. What is the closing cash balance?

whyNot.D: ₦270,000 is the total of the receipts side only.
whyNot.B: ₦50,000 leaves out the opening balance of ₦85,000.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Ngozi owes Bright Stores ₦60,000. She pays within the credit period and is allowed a cash discount of 5%. How much cash does Bright Stores receive?
questions.explanation: Discount = 5% × ₦60,000 = ₦3,000. Cash received = ₦60,000 − ₦3,000 = ₦57,000. Her account is cleared by cash ₦57,000 plus discount allowed ₦3,000.

whyNot.B: ₦3,000 is the discount, not the cash received.
whyNot.C: ₦63,000 adds the discount instead of deducting it.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A business buys office furniture on credit from Ade Furniture Ltd. In which book of original entry is this first recorded?
questions.explanation: Furniture is a non-current asset, not goods for resale, so it does not go in the purchases journal. A credit purchase of a non-current asset is recorded in the journal proper: debit furniture, credit Ade Furniture Ltd.

whyNot.C: The purchases journal is only for credit purchases of goods meant for resale.
whyNot.B: No cash or cheque was paid, so the cash book is not used.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: On 31 March Ibrahim's cash book shows a debit bank balance of ₦245,000. Cheques of ₦38,000 sent to suppliers have not yet been presented, and a deposit of ₦22,500 has not yet been credited by the bank. What balance should the bank statement show?
questions.explanation: Start with the cash book balance. Unpresented cheques have reduced the cash book but not the bank, so add them: ₦245,000 + ₦38,000 = ₦283,000. Uncredited deposits have increased the cash book but not the bank, so subtract them: ₦283,000 − ₦22,500 = ₦260,500.

whyNot.A: ₦229,500 reverses both adjustments (subtracts the cheques, adds the deposit).
whyNot.B: ₦305,500 adds both items.
whyNot.C: ₦184,500 subtracts both items.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: While preparing a bank reconciliation, a cashier finds bank charges on the bank statement that are not yet in the cash book. How should the cash book be updated?
options: Credit the bank column of the cash book
Add the charges to the bank statement balance
Show them as an unpresented cheque
Debit the bank column of the cash book
questions.explanation: Bank charges reduce the money in the account. The bank has already deducted them, so the cash book is brought up to date by entering them on the credit (payments) side of the bank column, with the debit to bank charges account.

whyNot.D: A debit would increase the bank balance, but charges reduce it.
whyNot.B: The bank statement is already correct; it is the cash book that is incomplete.
whyNot.C: Unpresented cheques are payments in the cash book not yet on the statement — the opposite situation.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The debit side of Tunde's account in the sales ledger totals ₦180,000 and the credit side totals ₦125,000. What is the balance brought down?
questions.explanation: The balance is the difference between the two sides: ₦180,000 − ₦125,000 = ₦55,000. The balance carried down is placed on the smaller (credit) side, so the balance brought down appears on the debit side: Tunde owes ₦55,000.

whyNot.C: The balance c/d is entered on the credit side, but the balance b/d goes on the opposite (debit) side.
whyNot.B: ₦305,000 adds the two sides instead of finding the difference.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: What is the main purpose of preparing a trial balance?
options: To show the financial position at a given date
To record transactions for the first time
To show the profit or loss for the period
To check the arithmetical accuracy of the double-entry postings
questions.explanation: A trial balance lists all ledger balances. If total debits equal total credits, the double entry is arithmetically correct (although some errors can still be hidden). It also helps in preparing final accounts.

whyNot.C: Profit or loss is shown in the income statement (trading and profit and loss account).
whyNot.A: Financial position is shown in the statement of financial position (balance sheet).

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Goods sold on credit to Musa Bello were posted to the account of Musa Bala. What type of error is this?
questions.explanation: An error of commission is when the correct amount is posted to the correct side but in the wrong account of the same class — here the wrong personal account. The trial balance still agrees.

whyNot.C: An error of principle puts an item in the wrong class of account, e.g. an asset treated as an expense.
whyNot.B: An error of original entry is a wrong amount entered in the book of original entry.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The cost of a new delivery van was debited to motor expenses account. What type of error is this?
questions.explanation: A van is a non-current asset (capital expenditure), but it was treated as an expense (revenue expenditure). Posting to the wrong class of account is an error of principle.

whyNot.A: An error of commission uses the wrong account of the same class, such as the wrong customer's account.
whyNot.D: An error of omission means the transaction was not recorded at all.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A trial balance has debit totals of ₦452,300 and credit totals of ₦447,800. A suspense account is opened to make it agree. What is the balance on the suspense account?
questions.explanation: Difference = ₦452,300 − ₦447,800 = ₦4,500. The credit side is short, so ₦4,500 is entered on the credit side of the trial balance as a suspense account credit balance.

whyNot.D: The suspense balance goes on the side that is short; here the credit side is smaller.
whyNot.B: ₦900,100 adds the two totals together.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The sales journal was undercast by ₦2,000, and the total was posted to the sales account. Customers' accounts were posted correctly. What entry corrects this error?
questions.explanation: Undercast means the total was ₦2,000 too small, so the sales account was credited with ₦2,000 too little. Only one side was wrong, so the difference sits in suspense. Correct it by crediting sales ₦2,000 and debiting suspense ₦2,000.

whyNot.D: This reverses the correction and would make sales even smaller.
whyNot.B: The customers' accounts were already correct, so receivables need no change.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Wages were overstated by ₦5,000 in the wages account and sales were also overstated by ₦5,000 in the sales account, so the trial balance still agreed. What type of error is this?
questions.explanation: Compensating errors are two or more errors that cancel each other out. An extra ₦5,000 debit (wages) is balanced by an extra ₦5,000 credit (sales), so the totals still agree.

whyNot.C: Omission means a transaction was not recorded at all.
whyNot.B: No item was put in the wrong class of account.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: From the following, find the closing balance on the sales ledger control account: opening debit balance ₦120,000; credit sales ₦450,000; cash received from customers ₦380,000; discount allowed ₦9,000; returns inwards ₦12,000; bad debts written off ₦4,000.

whyNot.A: ₦190,000 is the opening balance plus credit sales minus cash received only; discounts, returns and bad debts are also credits.
whyNot.C: ₦174,000 leaves out the discount allowed of ₦9,000.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following appears on the debit side of a purchases ledger control account?
questions.explanation: The purchases ledger control account summarises amounts owed to suppliers. Anything that reduces the amount owed — payments, returns outwards and discount received — goes on the debit side.

whyNot.D: Credit purchases increase what is owed, so they are credited.
whyNot.A: Amounts owed to suppliers are a credit balance, so the opening balance is on the credit side.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Discount allowed of ₦1,200 was correctly entered in the customer's account but was entered on the credit side of the discount allowed account. What effect does this have on the trial balance?
questions.explanation: The correct entry was debit discount allowed ₦1,200, credit customer ₦1,200. Instead both were credits. The debits lost ₦1,200 and the credits gained ₦1,200, so credits now exceed debits by 2 × ₦1,200 = ₦2,400.

whyNot.A: The extra amount is on the credit side, not the debit side.
whyNot.B: Entering on the wrong side doubles the difference: one side loses ₦1,200 and the other gains ₦1,200.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Cash sales of ₦8,000 were debited to the sales account and credited to the cash account. What journal entry corrects this error?
questions.explanation: This is a complete reversal of entries. Cash was wrongly reduced by ₦8,000 and must also be increased by ₦8,000, so cash needs a debit of ₦16,000. Sales needs a credit of ₦16,000 for the same reason. No suspense entry is needed because the trial balance agreed.

whyNot.C: ₦8,000 only cancels the wrong entry; another ₦8,000 is needed to make the correct entry.
whyNot.D: This would double the error.
whyNot.A: A complete reversal does not upset the trial balance, so suspense is not involved.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: From the following, calculate the cost of sales: opening inventory ₦75,000; purchases ₦420,000; carriage inwards ₦8,000; returns outwards ₦12,000; closing inventory ₦90,000.
questions.explanation: Cost of sales = opening inventory + purchases + carriage inwards − returns outwards − closing inventory = ₦75,000 + ₦420,000 + ₦8,000 − ₦12,000 − ₦90,000 = ₦401,000.

whyNot.A: ₦425,000 adds returns outwards instead of deducting them.
whyNot.C: ₦385,000 deducts carriage inwards, which is part of the cost of purchases.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Kemi's sales for the year were ₦650,000 and returns inwards were ₦15,000. Her cost of sales was ₦410,000. What was her gross profit?
questions.explanation: Net sales = ₦650,000 − ₦15,000 = ₦635,000. Gross profit = net sales − cost of sales = ₦635,000 − ₦410,000 = ₦225,000.

whyNot.A: ₦240,000 ignores the returns inwards.
whyNot.C: ₦255,000 adds the returns inwards to sales instead of deducting them.
whyNot.D: ₦635,000 is net sales (turnover), not gross profit.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A machine cost ₦1,200,000 and is expected to last 5 years with a residual value of ₦200,000. What is the annual depreciation charge using the straight-line method?
questions.explanation: Straight-line depreciation = (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life = (₦1,200,000 − ₦200,000) ÷ 5 = ₦1,000,000 ÷ 5 = ₦200,000 per year.

whyNot.C: ₦240,000 is cost ÷ 5; it ignores the residual value.
whyNot.B: ₦1,000,000 is the total depreciable amount over all 5 years.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A generator bought for ₦800,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum on the reducing balance method. What is the depreciation charge for the second year?

whyNot.C: ₦160,000 is the first year's charge; under reducing balance the charge falls each year.
whyNot.D: ₦320,000 is the total for two years on the straight-line basis.
whyNot.A: ₦512,000 is the net book value at the end of year 2.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A business's annual rent is ₦360,000. By the year end it had paid only ₦330,000. What amount of rent should be charged in the profit and loss account for the year?
questions.explanation: Under the accruals concept, the expense charged is the amount for the whole year, ₦360,000, whether paid or not. The unpaid ₦30,000 (₦360,000 − ₦330,000) is shown as an accrued expense under current liabilities.

whyNot.A: ₦330,000 is the cash paid; it leaves out the rent owing.
whyNot.B: ₦30,000 is the accrual, which is shown in the statement of financial position.
whyNot.C: ₦390,000 adds the accrual to the full year's rent, counting it twice.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Insurance paid in advance at the end of the financial year is shown in the statement of financial position as
questions.explanation: A prepayment is a benefit the business has paid for but not yet used; the insurer owes it cover for the coming period. It is therefore an asset, and since it will be used within a year it is a current asset.

whyNot.A: An expense owing (accrual) is a current liability; a prepayment is the opposite.
whyNot.C: Prepaid insurance will be used up within a year, so it is not non-current.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: In the final accounts of a trader, carriage outwards is treated as
options: a deduction from sales in the trading account
an expense in the profit and loss account
an addition to purchases in the trading account
questions.explanation: Carriage outwards is the cost of delivering goods to customers. It is a selling and distribution expense, charged in the profit and loss section, not part of the cost of buying goods.

whyNot.D: That is the treatment of carriage inwards, which is part of the cost of purchases.
whyNot.A: Only returns inwards are deducted from sales.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: At the year end, trade receivables are ₦240,000. The allowance for doubtful debts is to be kept at 5% of receivables. The existing allowance is ₦9,000. What amount is charged to the profit and loss account?
questions.explanation: Required allowance = 5% × ₦240,000 = ₦12,000. An allowance of ₦9,000 already exists, so only the increase is charged: ₦12,000 − ₦9,000 = ₦3,000.

whyNot.B: ₦12,000 is the new total allowance; only the increase is charged this year.
whyNot.D: ₦21,000 adds the old and new allowances together.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Akin Traders has current assets of ₦360,000 and current liabilities of ₦150,000. What is its current ratio?
questions.explanation: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = ₦360,000 ÷ ₦150,000 = 2.4, written 2.4 : 1. The business has ₦2.40 of current assets for every ₦1 of current liabilities.

whyNot.A: 0.42 : 1 divides current liabilities by current assets, the wrong way round.
whyNot.B: 1.4 : 1 divides working capital (₦210,000) by current liabilities; the current ratio uses total current assets.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A business made a gross profit of ₦180,000 on sales of ₦600,000. What is its gross profit margin?
questions.explanation: Gross profit margin = gross profit ÷ sales × 100 = ₦180,000 ÷ ₦600,000 × 100 = 30%.

whyNot.A: 42.9% is the mark-up: gross profit ÷ cost of sales (₦180,000 ÷ ₦420,000).
whyNot.C: 70% is cost of sales as a percentage of sales.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Where there is no partnership agreement, the Partnership Act 1890 provides that profits and losses are shared
options: in the ratio of hours worked
questions.explanation: In the absence of an agreement, the Partnership Act 1890 says partners share profits and losses equally, receive no interest on capital and no salaries, and are paid 5% interest on loans they make to the firm.

whyNot.B: Sharing in the ratio of capitals is common but must be agreed; it is not the default rule.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Under the partnership agreement, interest on capital is allowed at 5% per annum. Adaeze's capital is ₦2,000,000. How much interest on capital is she credited with for the year?
questions.explanation: Interest on capital = 5% × ₦2,000,000 = 0.05 × ₦2,000,000 = ₦100,000. It is debited to the appropriation account and credited to her current account.

whyNot.C: ₦10,000 is 0.5%, a slip with the decimal point.
whyNot.A: ₦200,000 is 10% of the capital.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Ali and Bayo share profits and losses in the ratio 3 : 1. Net profit for the year is ₦900,000. Interest on capital: Ali ₦60,000, Bayo ₦40,000. Bayo receives a salary of ₦120,000. Interest on drawings: Ali ₦10,000, Bayo ₦6,000. What is Ali's share of the residual profit?
questions.explanation: Residual profit = net profit + interest on drawings − interest on capital − salary = ₦900,000 + ₦16,000 − ₦100,000 − ₦120,000 = ₦696,000. Ali's share = 3/4 × ₦696,000 = ₦522,000.

whyNot.B: ₦498,000 deducts interest on drawings instead of adding it (residual ₦664,000).
whyNot.C: ₦675,000 is 3/4 of the full net profit before appropriations.
whyNot.D: ₦174,000 is Bayo's 1/4 share.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Uche's current account had an opening credit balance of ₦50,000. During the year his share of profit was ₦300,000, his interest on capital ₦40,000, his drawings ₦210,000 and interest on drawings ₦7,000. What is the closing balance on his current account?

whyNot.A: ₦187,000 adds interest on drawings instead of deducting it.
whyNot.C: ₦133,000 leaves out the interest on capital of ₦40,000.
whyNot.D: ₦607,000 adds the drawings and interest on drawings instead of deducting them.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: In partnership accounts, interest charged on a partner's drawings is
options: credited to the partner's capital account
debited to the appropriation account and credited to the partner's current account
credited to the appropriation account and debited to the partner's current account
debited to the profit and loss account as an expense
questions.explanation: Interest on drawings is a charge on the partner, so it reduces what the partner is owed (debit current account) and adds to the profit available for sharing (credit appropriation account).

whyNot.B: That is the treatment of interest on capital, which benefits the partner.
whyNot.D: Appropriations between partners are not business expenses.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Zenith Foods Plc issues 200,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each at ₦1.50 per share. All the money is received. How much is credited to the share premium account?
questions.explanation: The premium is the amount above nominal value: ₦1.50 − ₦1.00 = ₦0.50 per share. Share premium = 200,000 × ₦0.50 = ₦100,000. The nominal value, ₦200,000, goes to ordinary share capital.

whyNot.D: ₦300,000 is the total cash received.
whyNot.A: ₦200,000 is the nominal value credited to share capital.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following best describes preference shares?
options: They carry the main voting rights in the company
They receive a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid
They are loans to the company that must be repaid with interest
Their dividend rises and falls with the company's profits
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders are entitled to a fixed percentage dividend, paid before any dividend goes to ordinary shareholders. They usually have limited or no voting rights.

whyNot.A: Ordinary shareholders normally hold the voting rights.
whyNot.C: That describes debentures, which are loans, not shares.
whyNot.D: A dividend that varies with profit is typical of ordinary shares.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: How is interest on debentures treated in a company's financial statements?
options: As an appropriation of profit like a dividend
As an expense charged in arriving at profit
As an addition to share capital
As a deduction from share premium
questions.explanation: Debenture holders are lenders, not owners. The interest they receive is a cost of borrowing, so it is charged as an expense (finance cost) before profit is found, and it must be paid whether or not a profit is made.

whyNot.A: Dividends are appropriations to owners; debenture interest is paid to lenders.
whyNot.C: Debentures are loans and are shown as liabilities, not share capital.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A company has 500,000 ordinary shares of ₦2 each, fully paid. The directors declare an ordinary dividend of 10%. What is the total dividend?
questions.explanation: Dividend percentages are based on nominal (issued) share capital. Share capital = 500,000 × ₦2 = ₦1,000,000. Dividend = 10% × ₦1,000,000 = ₦100,000.

whyNot.C: ₦50,000 is 10% of the number of shares, ignoring the ₦2 nominal value.
whyNot.A: ₦1,000,000 is the share capital itself.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: In Nigerian public sector accounting, the main fund into which the Federal Government's revenues are paid, and from which approved spending is made, is the
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution provides for a Consolidated Revenue Fund of the Federation into which all revenues of the Federal Government are paid, except where a law directs otherwise. Spending from it must be authorised by law, usually an Appropriation Act.

whyNot.A: The Contingencies Fund is a small fund for urgent, unforeseen spending.
whyNot.C: A sinking fund is set aside to repay a specific loan.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Hauwa's business has capital of ₦1,500,000 and liabilities of ₦420,000. What is the value of its total assets?
questions.explanation: Assets = Capital + Liabilities = ₦1,500,000 + ₦420,000 = ₦1,920,000.

whyNot.B: ₦1,080,000 subtracts liabilities from capital; assets are financed by both.
whyNot.A: ₦1,500,000 is capital only.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The skill and loyalty of a firm's workers are not recorded in its books. Which concept explains this?
questions.explanation: Under the money measurement concept, only items that can be measured reliably in money are recorded. Staff skill and loyalty have value but cannot be measured in naira, so they are not recorded.

whyNot.A: Going concern is the assumption that the business will continue to operate.
whyNot.D: Accruals concerns recognising income and expenses in the period they arise.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The idea that every business transaction has two aspects, one debit and one credit of equal amount, is known as the
questions.explanation: The duality (dual aspect) concept is the basis of double entry: every transaction affects at least two accounts, with equal debits and credits, which keeps the accounting equation in balance.

whyNot.D: Realisation is about when revenue is earned.
whyNot.B: Materiality is about the significance of an item.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Land bought for ₦5,000,000 ten years ago is still shown in the books at ₦5,000,000, although it is now worth much more. Which concept is being applied?
questions.explanation: The historical cost concept records assets at what they actually cost when acquired. The original cost is objective and can be verified from documents, so the land stays at ₦5,000,000.

whyNot.A: Realisation deals with when revenue is recognised, not the value of land.
whyNot.C: Business entity separates the owner from the business.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A customer orders goods in May, they are delivered and invoiced in June, and payment is received in July. Under the realisation concept, in which month is the sale recognised?
options: Spread over May, June and July
questions.explanation: Under the realisation concept, revenue is recognised when the goods pass to the customer and the customer becomes liable to pay — on delivery and invoicing in June — not when the order is placed or when cash arrives.

whyNot.C: An order alone is not a sale; no goods have changed hands.
whyNot.A: Receiving cash in July settles the debt, but the sale was already earned in June.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which user of accounting information is mainly interested in whether a business can repay a loan with interest when it falls due?
options: A customer buying goods for cash
A competitor in the same market
A bank that lends to the business
questions.explanation: Lenders such as banks want to know if the business will be able to pay interest and repay the loan, so they study its liquidity, profitability and the security available.

whyNot.A: A cash customer has no money at risk with the business.
whyNot.C: A competitor may be curious about performance but is not owed any money.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The owner of a provision store takes goods from the shop for use at home. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
questions.explanation: The inventory taken is a drawing. The business loses an asset (inventory goes down), and the owner's claim on the business (capital) falls by the same amount. The entry is debit drawings, credit purchases.

whyNot.D: No debt is paid, so liabilities are unchanged.
whyNot.C: Taking goods creates no new debt for the business.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A business pays a supplier ₦25,000 by cheque to settle an amount owed. What is the effect on the accounting equation?
questions.explanation: The bank balance (an asset) falls by ₦25,000 and the amount owed to the supplier (a liability) falls by ₦25,000. Capital is not affected because no profit, loss or drawing is involved.

whyNot.C: Paying a debt is not an expense or a drawing, so capital does not change.
whyNot.B: Settling a debt does not create profit, so capital does not rise.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Gabriel's business has premises ₦2,400,000, equipment ₦650,000, inventory ₦310,000 and cash ₦140,000. It owes trade payables ₦270,000 and a bank loan of ₦900,000. What is Gabriel's capital?

whyNot.A: ₦3,500,000 is total assets before deducting liabilities.
whyNot.C: ₦3,230,000 deducts only the trade payables.
whyNot.D: ₦2,600,000 deducts only the bank loan.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A sole trader's capital was ₦800,000 at the start of the year and ₦1,020,000 at the end. She took drawings of ₦150,000 and brought in no new capital. What was her profit for the year?
questions.explanation: Closing capital = opening capital + profit − drawings, so profit = closing capital − opening capital + drawings = ₦1,020,000 − ₦800,000 + ₦150,000 = ₦370,000.

whyNot.D: ₦220,000 is only the increase in capital; drawings must be added back because they reduced capital.
whyNot.B: ₦70,000 subtracts drawings instead of adding them back.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which source document is used to record a credit sale in the sales journal?
questions.explanation: When goods are sold on credit the seller sends the buyer an invoice showing the goods, quantities and amount. A copy of this sales invoice is the source document for the sales journal.

whyNot.A: A receipt is issued when cash is received, not for a credit sale.
whyNot.C: A cheque counterfoil records a payment made by cheque.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: When a customer returns goods bought on credit, the seller sends the customer a
questions.explanation: A credit note tells the customer that their account has been credited (reduced) by the value of the goods returned. The seller records it in the returns inwards journal.

whyNot.A: A debit note is sent by a buyer to a supplier when returning goods or claiming an allowance.
whyNot.C: A statement of account summarises all transactions for the period; it is not issued for one return.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A trader pays ₦50,000 of office cash into the business bank account. How is this recorded in a two-column cash book?
options: Record it in the journal proper only
Credit the cash column and debit the bank column (a contra entry)
Debit the cash column and credit the bank column
Debit both the cash and bank columns
questions.explanation: Cash leaves the office (credit cash column) and enters the bank (debit bank column). Both entries are in the same cash book, so it is called a contra entry and is marked 'C'.

whyNot.C: That is the entry for withdrawing cash from the bank for office use.
whyNot.A: Both accounts are in the cash book itself, so the journal is not needed.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A petty cashier is given an imprest of ₦30,000. At the end of the month ₦6,750 remains in the petty cash box. How much is needed to restore the imprest?
questions.explanation: Amount spent = imprest − cash left = ₦30,000 − ₦6,750 = ₦23,250. Under the imprest system the cashier reimburses exactly this amount, bringing the float back to ₦30,000.

whyNot.D: ₦6,750 is the cash still in hand.
whyNot.A: ₦36,750 adds the balance left to the imprest.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The total of the discount allowed column in the cash book is posted to the
options: credit side of discount allowed account
debit side of discount received account
credit side of the sales account
debit side of discount allowed account
questions.explanation: Discount allowed is an expense of the business. Each customer's account has already been credited individually, so the column total is debited to discount allowed account to complete the double entry.

whyNot.A: Expenses are debited, not credited.
whyNot.B: Discount received is a different account, for discounts given to the business by suppliers.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Kunle settles a debt owed to Obi Enterprises within the discount period and is allowed 2% cash discount. Obi Enterprises receives a cheque for ₦78,400. How much discount was allowed?

whyNot.A: ₦1,568 is 2% of the cheque amount, but discount is calculated on the debt before deduction.
whyNot.B: ₦80,000 is the original debt, not the discount.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Yemi's bank statement shows a favourable balance of ₦182,000. Cheques of ₦47,500 she issued have not been presented, and deposits of ₦31,000 have not yet been credited by the bank. What is the bank balance in her cash book?
questions.explanation: Start from the bank statement. Unpresented cheques have already reduced the cash book, so deduct them: ₦182,000 − ₦47,500 = ₦134,500. Uncredited deposits are already in the cash book, so add them: ₦134,500 + ₦31,000 = ₦165,500.

whyNot.C: ₦198,500 adds the cheques and deducts the deposits — the reverse adjustments.
whyNot.D: ₦260,500 adds both items.
whyNot.B: ₦103,500 deducts both items.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A customer pays a debt directly into the business's bank account by transfer. It appears on the bank statement but not in the cash book. How is the cash book updated?
options: Deduct it from the bank statement balance only
Debit the bank column and credit the customer's account
Debit the cash column and credit sales
Credit the bank column and debit the customer's account
questions.explanation: A direct credit increases the money in the bank. The cash book is updated by debiting the bank column, with the credit going to the customer's account because the debt is reduced.

whyNot.D: This would reduce the bank balance and increase the customer's debt.
whyNot.C: The money went into the bank, and it settles a debt rather than being a new sale.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: In which ledger are the personal accounts of credit customers kept?
questions.explanation: The sales ledger (receivables ledger) holds a personal account for each credit customer, showing what each owes the business.

whyNot.B: The purchases ledger holds the accounts of credit suppliers.
whyNot.C: The general (nominal) ledger holds impersonal accounts such as sales, wages and assets.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A cheque received from a customer and paid into the bank is later returned by the bank marked 'refer to drawer' (dishonoured). What entry records the dishonour?
options: Debit the bank column of the cash book; credit the customer's account
Debit bad debts; credit the customer's account
Debit the customer's account; credit sales
Debit the customer's account; credit the bank column of the cash book
questions.explanation: When the cheque was received, bank was debited and the customer credited. A dishonoured cheque means no money was actually received, so the entry is reversed: credit bank and debit the customer, who owes the money again.

whyNot.A: This is the original entry for receiving the cheque, not its reversal.
whyNot.B: The debt is not yet written off as bad; the customer is simply still owing.
whyNot.C: No new sale has taken place.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: An invoice for ₦7,200 was entered in the sales journal as ₦7,000 and posted from there to the customer's account and to sales. What type of error is this?
questions.explanation: An error of original entry occurs when a wrong amount is entered in the book of original entry. Both the debit and the credit are posted with the same wrong figure, so the trial balance still agrees.

whyNot.C: The sale was recorded, though with the wrong figure, so nothing was omitted.
whyNot.A: The correct accounts were used, so it is not an error of commission.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A sales invoice was lost and the sale was never entered in the books. What type of error is this?
questions.explanation: An error of omission occurs when a transaction is left out of the books completely. Neither the debit nor the credit is recorded, so the trial balance still agrees.

whyNot.B: An error of commission records the transaction but in the wrong account of the right class.
whyNot.C: An error of original entry records the transaction with a wrong amount.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A trial balance shows total debits of ₦615,000 and total credits of ₦628,400. What is the suspense account balance needed to make it agree?
questions.explanation: Difference = ₦628,400 − ₦615,000 = ₦13,400. The debit side is short, so a suspense account with a debit balance of ₦13,400 is opened.

whyNot.B: The suspense entry goes on the shorter side, which here is the debit side.
whyNot.C: ₦1,243,400 is the two totals added together.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Rent paid of ₦45,000 was correctly entered in the cash book but was posted to the rent account as ₦54,000. The difference was placed in suspense. What entry corrects the error?
questions.explanation: The rent account was debited ₦9,000 too much (₦54,000 − ₦45,000). To reduce it, credit rent ₦9,000. The other side of the correction clears the suspense account: debit suspense ₦9,000.

whyNot.A: Debiting rent would make the overstatement worse.
whyNot.B: Only the excess of ₦9,000 needs correcting, not the whole posting.
whyNot.C: The cash book entry was already correct.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Goods of ₦30,000 bought on credit from Ade were correctly debited to purchases, but were also debited (instead of credited) to Ade's account. What effect does this have on the trial balance?
questions.explanation: The credit of ₦30,000 to Ade was missing and an extra debit of ₦30,000 was made. Debits are therefore ₦30,000 too high and credits ₦30,000 too low, a gap of ₦30,000 × 2 = ₦60,000 with debits larger.

whyNot.D: Putting an entry on the wrong side doubles the difference.
whyNot.A: The extra amount is on the debit side.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The cost of repairing a machine was debited to the machinery account. Which entry corrects this error?
options: Debit repairs account; credit machinery account
Debit suspense account; credit machinery account
Debit machinery account; credit repairs account
Debit repairs account; credit suspense account
questions.explanation: Repairs are revenue expenditure, but the cost was treated as capital (an error of principle). The machinery account must be reduced (credited) and the repairs expense increased (debited). The trial balance was not affected, so suspense is not used.

whyNot.C: This would add even more to the machinery account.
whyNot.D: An error of principle does not affect the trial balance, so there is no suspense entry.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Calculate the closing balance on the purchases ledger control account from: opening credit balance ₦95,000; credit purchases ₦380,000; payments to suppliers ₦310,000; discount received ₦6,500; returns outwards ₦8,500.

whyNot.B: ₦165,000 ignores the discount received and returns outwards.
whyNot.C: ₦135,000 deducts the discount received and returns outwards twice.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT appear in a sales ledger control account?
questions.explanation: The sales ledger control account summarises the accounts of credit customers. Cash sales involve no debtor, so they never pass through it. Credit sales are debited; returns inwards and bad debts are credited.

whyNot.A: Credit sales increase what customers owe and are debited to the control account.
whyNot.B: Returns inwards reduce what customers owe and are credited to it.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following balances appears on the credit side of a trial balance?
questions.explanation: Credit balances are liabilities, capital, income and gains. Discount received is income, so it is a credit balance. Drawings, expenses like carriage inwards, and assets like receivables are debit balances.

whyNot.D: Drawings reduce capital and are a debit balance.
whyNot.A: Carriage inwards is an expense, a debit balance.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: After the final accounts were prepared, it was found that closing inventory had been overstated by ₦20,000. What effect did this have on gross profit?
questions.explanation: Closing inventory is deducted in finding cost of sales. If it is ₦20,000 too high, cost of sales is ₦20,000 too low, so gross profit (sales − cost of sales) is ₦20,000 too high.

whyNot.C: A higher closing inventory lowers cost of sales, which raises profit, not lowers it.
whyNot.A: The error affects only the closing inventory once, so the effect is ₦20,000.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Yusuf's gross profit is ₦380,000. His expenses are salaries ₦120,000, rent ₦60,000 and depreciation ₦35,000. He also received discount of ₦8,000. What is his net profit?

whyNot.B: ₦157,000 treats discount received as an expense instead of income.
whyNot.D: ₦165,000 ignores the discount received.
whyNot.C: ₦215,000 is the total of the expenses.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Office equipment cost ₦900,000 and is depreciated at 10% per annum on the straight-line method, with no residual value. What is its net book value after 3 years?
questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = 10% × ₦900,000 = ₦90,000. After 3 years accumulated depreciation = 3 × ₦90,000 = ₦270,000. Net book value = ₦900,000 − ₦270,000 = ₦630,000.

whyNot.D: ₦656,100 uses the reducing balance method (₦900,000 × 0.9³).
whyNot.B: ₦270,000 is the accumulated depreciation, not the net book value.
whyNot.A: ₦810,000 is the net book value after only 1 year.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A tricycle costing ₦500,000 is depreciated at 25% per annum on the reducing balance method. What is its net book value at the end of the second year?

whyNot.C: ₦250,000 uses straight line (₦125,000 each year).
whyNot.A: ₦375,000 is the NBV after only one year.
whyNot.B: ₦218,750 is the total depreciation for the two years.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A machine that cost ₦400,000 had accumulated depreciation of ₦260,000 when it was sold for ₦120,000. What was the result of the disposal?
questions.explanation: Net book value at disposal = ₦400,000 − ₦260,000 = ₦140,000. Sale proceeds of ₦120,000 are less than the NBV, so there is a loss of ₦140,000 − ₦120,000 = ₦20,000.

whyNot.B: The proceeds are below the book value, so it is a loss, not a profit.
whyNot.A: ₦140,000 is the net book value, not the loss.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following is capital expenditure?
options: Cost of installing a newly bought machine
Cost of servicing a delivery van
questions.explanation: Capital expenditure is spending to acquire a non-current asset or bring it into use. Installation is needed before the machine can work, so it is added to the machine's cost. The others are day-to-day running costs (revenue expenditure).

whyNot.A: Operators' wages are a running cost of the period.
whyNot.D: Servicing maintains the van; it does not create or improve an asset.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: At the year end a landlord has received rent from a tenant for the first two months of next year. In the landlord's statement of financial position this is shown as
options: income in the current year's profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Rent received in advance has not yet been earned; the landlord owes the tenant two months' use of the property. It is income received in advance, a current liability.

whyNot.D: Rent owed to the landlord (in arrears) would be a current asset; this is the reverse.
whyNot.B: Under the accruals concept, it belongs to next year's income.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-current asset of a supermarket?
questions.explanation: Non-current assets are held for long-term use in the business, not for resale. A delivery van is used for several years. Inventory, receivables and cash are current assets that change quickly.

whyNot.D: Inventory is held for resale, so it is a current asset.
whyNot.B: Receivables are expected to be collected within a year.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A business has current assets of ₦420,000, including inventory of ₦180,000. Its current liabilities are ₦160,000. What is its acid test (quick) ratio?
questions.explanation: The acid test ratio leaves out inventory: (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = (₦420,000 − ₦180,000) ÷ ₦160,000 = ₦240,000 ÷ ₦160,000 = 1.5 : 1.

whyNot.B: 2.63 : 1 is the current ratio, which includes inventory.
whyNot.A: 1.13 : 1 divides the inventory (₦180,000) by current liabilities; the quick assets are the current assets other than inventory.
whyNot.D: 0.67 : 1 divides the wrong way round.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Cost of sales for the year was ₦600,000. Opening inventory was ₦70,000 and closing inventory was ₦50,000. What is the rate of inventory turnover?
questions.explanation: Average inventory = (₦70,000 + ₦50,000) ÷ 2 = ₦60,000. Rate of inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory = ₦600,000 ÷ ₦60,000 = 10 times.

whyNot.A: 12 times uses closing inventory only.
whyNot.D: 8.6 times uses opening inventory only.
whyNot.C: 5 times divides by the total of the two inventories instead of their average.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A trader adds a mark-up of 25% to cost. If her cost of sales for the month is ₦300,000, what are her sales?
questions.explanation: Mark-up is calculated on cost. Gross profit = 25% × ₦300,000 = ₦75,000. Sales = cost + gross profit = ₦300,000 + ₦75,000 = ₦375,000.

whyNot.A: ₦400,000 treats 25% as a margin on sales (₦300,000 ÷ 0.75).
whyNot.B: ₦225,000 deducts the mark-up instead of adding it.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: In partnership accounts, a salary paid to a partner is shown in the
options: profit and loss account as wages
statement of financial position as a liability
questions.explanation: A partner is an owner, not an employee. A partner's salary is a way of sharing profit, so it is debited in the appropriation account (and credited to the partner's current account), not charged as an expense.

whyNot.B: The trading account deals only with sales and cost of sales.
whyNot.A: Only employees' wages are expenses in the profit and loss account.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Ese and Femi are partners with capitals of ₦1,500,000 and ₦900,000. Interest on capital is allowed at 8% per annum. What is the total interest on capital?

whyNot.D: ₦120,000 is Ese's interest only.
whyNot.A: ₦72,000 is Femi's interest only.
whyNot.B: ₦240,000 is 10%, not 8%, of total capital.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Kola and Lami share residual profit in the ratio 2 : 3. The residual profit for the year is ₦450,000. What is Lami's share?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5. Lami's share = 3/5 × ₦450,000 = ₦270,000 (and Kola gets 2/5 = ₦180,000).

whyNot.D: ₦180,000 is Kola's 2/5 share.
whyNot.C: ₦225,000 shares the profit equally.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A partner withdrew ₦240,000 at the start of the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 5% per annum. How much interest on drawings is charged for the full year?
questions.explanation: The money was out of the business for the whole year, so interest on drawings = 5% × ₦240,000 × 1 = ₦12,000. It is debited to the partner's current account and credited to the appropriation account.

whyNot.A: ₦24,000 is 10% of the drawings.
whyNot.D: ₦6,000 would be interest for only six months.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: When partners keep fixed capital accounts, where are their shares of profit and their drawings recorded?
questions.explanation: Under the fixed capital method, capital accounts show only the agreed capital. Shares of profit, interest, salaries and drawings all go through the current accounts, whose balances change each year.

whyNot.B: That is the fluctuating capital method; with fixed capitals these accounts stay unchanged.
whyNot.C: A realisation account is used only when a partnership is dissolved.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The maximum amount of share capital that a company is permitted to issue is called its
questions.explanation: Authorised capital (registered capital) is the upper limit of shares a company may issue, as stated in its constitution. Issued, called-up and paid-up capital are parts of it.

whyNot.B: Issued capital is the part of authorised capital actually given to shareholders.
whyNot.C: Paid-up capital is the amount shareholders have actually paid.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A company issued 400,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each and has called up 75 kobo per share. Shareholders have paid ₦280,000. What is the amount of calls in arrear?
questions.explanation: Called-up capital = 400,000 × ₦0.75 = ₦300,000. Calls in arrear = called-up − paid = ₦300,000 − ₦280,000 = ₦20,000.

whyNot.C: ₦120,000 compares the full nominal value (₦400,000) with the amount paid.
whyNot.B: ₦100,000 is the uncalled capital (25 kobo per share).
whyNot.A: ₦300,000 is the called-up capital.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: A company's profit after tax is ₦750,000. It pays an 8% dividend on ₦1,000,000 of preference share capital and an ordinary dividend of ₦300,000. How much profit is retained?

whyNot.A: ₦450,000 ignores the preference dividend.
whyNot.D: ₦670,000 ignores the ordinary dividend.
whyNot.B: ₦380,000 is the total dividends paid.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: The document that sets out a government's estimated revenue and expenditure for a financial year is called the
questions.explanation: In public sector accounting, the budget (annual estimates) shows how much revenue the government expects and how it plans to spend it. Once passed by the legislature, it becomes law as the Appropriation Act.

whyNot.A: A bank reconciliation statement explains the difference between the cash book and the bank statement.
whyNot.D: A statement of affairs is used to find a sole trader's capital from incomplete records.

questions.subject: financial-accounting
questions.stem: Which of the following is a main difference between public sector accounting and accounting for a business?
options: Government revenue comes only from the sale of goods
Government aims at service and accountability rather than making a profit
Government accounts do not record any expenditure
questions.explanation: A business keeps accounts mainly to measure profit for its owners. Government provides public services, so its accounts focus on showing that money was raised and spent as authorised by law (accountability and stewardship), not on profit.

whyNot.D: Government accounts record all expenditure in detail to show it was authorised.
whyNot.A: Public accounts are audited, for example by the Auditor-General.
whyNot.B: Government revenue comes mainly from taxes, oil revenue, fees and grants.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Where was Moses when God called him from the burning bush?
options: At Horeb, the mountain of God
questions.explanation: Exodus 3:1-4 says Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, when he led it to Horeb, the mountain of God. There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of a bush that burned but was not consumed.

whyNot.A: Mount Nebo is where Moses viewed the Promised Land just before his death (Deuteronomy 34:1), not where he was called.
whyNot.D: Moses had fled from Egypt to Midian years before his call (Exodus 2:15).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Jethro saw Moses judging the people alone from morning till evening. What did he advise Moses to do?
options: Choose able, God-fearing men to judge the minor cases
Hand over the leadership of Israel to Aaron
Let the elders of Midian settle the disputes
Send the people back to Egypt to be judged
questions.explanation: In Exodus 18:13-26 Jethro warned that the work was too heavy for Moses. He advised him to choose capable, trustworthy men who feared God, set them over groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens to judge small matters, and bring only the hard cases to Moses. This is an early lesson in delegation of duty.

whyNot.B: Jethro did not ask Moses to give up leadership; Moses stayed the leader and kept the hard cases.
whyNot.C: The judges were to be chosen from among the Israelites, not from Midian.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Why were the Israelites defeated in their first attack on Ai?
options: The priests had left the ark of the covenant at Gilgal
The people had married the daughters of Ai
Achan had taken some of the devoted things from Jericho
Joshua had refused to send spies to Ai
questions.explanation: Joshua 7 explains that Achan son of Carmi, of the tribe of Judah, secretly took a fine mantle, silver and a bar of gold from the things devoted to the LORD at Jericho. Because of this sin, Israel was routed at Ai. After Achan confessed and was punished, Israel defeated Ai (Joshua 8).

whyNot.D: Joshua did send men to spy out Ai before the first attack (Joshua 7:2).
whyNot.A: The defeat is linked to Achan's disobedience, not to where the ark was kept.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Who killed Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin, king of Canaan, after Deborah and Barak defeated his forces?
options: Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite
questions.explanation: Judges 4 tells how Deborah, a prophetess who judged Israel, summoned Barak to fight Sisera. Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite. While he slept she drove a tent peg through his temple (Judges 4:21), fulfilling Deborah's word that the honour would go to a woman.

whyNot.C: Deborah led and encouraged Israel but did not kill Sisera herself.
whyNot.D: Barak pursued Sisera but arrived at Jael's tent after Sisera was already dead (Judges 4:22).
whyNot.B: Gideon was a later judge who fought the Midianites, not Sisera.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: When the LORD called the boy Samuel at night, Eli told him how to answer. What was Samuel to say?
options: Here I am, for you called me
Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening
Woe is me, for I am too young
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 3 the LORD called Samuel three times and each time Samuel ran to Eli. Eli then realised it was the LORD and told Samuel to answer, 'Speak, LORD, for your servant hears' (1 Samuel 3:9-10). Samuel obeyed and received God's message about Eli's house.

whyNot.A: 'Here I am, for you called me' is what Samuel said to Eli when he wrongly thought Eli had called him.
whyNot.D: Pleading youth is associated with Jeremiah's call (Jeremiah 1:6), not Samuel's.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Which reason did the elders of Israel give Samuel when they asked for a king?
options: Samuel was old and his sons did not walk in his ways
The Philistines had captured the city of Jerusalem
Samuel had refused to judge the people any longer
The priests at Shiloh had asked for a king
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 8:1-5 records that Samuel's sons, Joel and Abijah, took bribes and perverted justice. The elders came to Samuel at Ramah and said that he was old and his sons did not follow his ways, so they wanted a king to judge them like all the nations.

whyNot.B: Jerusalem was captured later by David (2 Samuel 5), not by the Philistines at this time.
whyNot.C: Samuel did not refuse to judge; he was displeased by the request but prayed to the LORD about it.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: After Saul spared Agag and the best of the Amalekite animals, Samuel rebuked him. What was the main lesson of Samuel's rebuke in 1 Samuel 15:22?
options: Obedience to God is better than sacrifice
Enemy kings should be spared and kept as servants
Good animals should be given to the poor
Kings must offer sacrifices only at Shiloh
questions.explanation: God had commanded Saul to destroy the Amalekites completely, but Saul kept King Agag alive and saved the best livestock, claiming they were for sacrifice. Samuel replied that to obey is better than sacrifice and to listen is better than the fat of rams (1 Samuel 15:22). Because Saul rejected God's word, God rejected him as king.

whyNot.D: The rebuke was about disobedience, not the place of sacrifice.
whyNot.B: Sparing Agag was part of Saul's sin, so this is the opposite of the lesson.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Nathan told David a story of a rich man who took a poor man's only ewe lamb. What did this parable expose?
options: Saul's jealousy and attempts to kill David
David's plan to build a temple for the ark
Absalom's plot to take the throne from David
David's sin of taking Bathsheba and causing Uriah's death
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 12:1-7 David angrily condemned the rich man in Nathan's story. Nathan replied, 'You are the man.' The rich man stood for David, who had many wives yet took Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite, and arranged Uriah's death in battle (2 Samuel 11). The parable shows that even a king is accountable to God.

whyNot.B: Nathan spoke about the temple in 2 Samuel 7, without a parable about a lamb.
whyNot.C: Absalom's revolt came later and was not the subject of Nathan's parable.
whyNot.A: Saul's jealousy was against David; the parable condemned David's own act.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: When God appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and told him to ask for whatever he wanted, what did Solomon ask for?
options: Long life and many years on the throne
An understanding mind to govern the people
Riches and honour above all kings
The death of all his enemies
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 3:5-14 Solomon asked for an understanding mind to judge God's people and to discern between good and evil. God was pleased and gave him wisdom, and also gave him riches and honour which he had not asked for.

whyNot.A: God noted that Solomon did not ask for long life (1 Kings 3:11).
whyNot.C: Riches and honour were added by God as a gift; Solomon did not ask for them.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: What decision by Rehoboam at Shechem led directly to the revolt of the ten northern tribes?
options: He married many foreign wives who worshipped other gods
He refused to allow the people to sacrifice at the temple
He rejected the elders' advice and promised to make the people's burden heavier
He moved the ark of the covenant from Jerusalem to Shechem
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:1-16 says the people asked Rehoboam to lighten the heavy yoke Solomon had laid on them. The old men advised him to serve the people and speak kindly. He rejected this and followed the young men, saying his father chastised them with whips but he would use scorpions. Israel then rebelled and made Jeroboam king, leaving Rehoboam with Judah (and Benjamin).

whyNot.A: Marrying foreign wives was Solomon's sin (1 Kings 11), which was why God decided to divide the kingdom, but it was not Rehoboam's decision at Shechem.
whyNot.B: Stopping people from going to the temple was Jeroboam's later concern (1 Kings 12:26-28), not Rehoboam's.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: On Mount Carmel, Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal. How many prophets of Baal does 1 Kings 18 say were there?
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 18:19-22 Elijah asked Ahab to gather the 450 prophets of Baal (and 400 prophets of Asherah) to Mount Carmel. Elijah stood alone as a prophet of the LORD, and God answered him by fire.

whyNot.B: 400 is the number of the prophets of Asherah mentioned in 1 Kings 18:19, not of Baal.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: When Elijah fled from Jezebel and came to Horeb, how did God make His presence known to him?
options: In a great wind that broke the rocks
In a still small voice after the wind, earthquake and fire
In fire that came down and burned the altar
In a pillar of cloud over the cave
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:11-12 says a great wind, an earthquake and a fire passed by, but the LORD was not in them. After the fire came a still small voice (a low whisper), and Elijah covered his face and went out to meet God. God then gave him new tasks.

whyNot.A: The text says the LORD was not in the wind.
whyNot.C: Fire falling on the altar happened at Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:38), not at Horeb.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Before God called him to prophesy, what was Amos's occupation?
options: A member of a school of prophets
A herdsman and a dresser of sycamore trees
A scribe in the king's court
questions.explanation: Amos told Amaziah, 'I am no prophet, nor a prophet's son, but a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs' (Amos 7:14; see also Amos 1:1, which places him among the shepherds of Tekoa). God took him from following the flock and sent him to prophesy to Israel.

whyNot.A: Amaziah, not Amos, was the priest of Bethel (Amos 7:10).
whyNot.B: Amos denied being a professional prophet or a prophet's son.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Amos told Israel that God hated their feasts and offerings, and wanted justice to roll down like waters (Amos 5:21-24). What was Amos teaching?
options: Festivals should be held only in Jerusalem
Worship is worthless to God without justice and right living
Music should not be used in the worship of God
Israel should offer more sacrifices to please God
questions.explanation: Israel was busy with religious festivals while the rich oppressed the poor and perverted justice. In Amos 5:21-24 God rejects such worship and calls for justice and righteousness to flow like an ever-flowing stream. True religion must show itself in fair treatment of others.

whyNot.D: God was rejecting their offerings, not asking for more.
whyNot.C: God's dislike of their songs was because of injustice, not a ban on music itself.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Whom did the prophet Hosea marry at God's command?
questions.explanation: Hosea 1:2-3 says the LORD told Hosea to take a wife who would be unfaithful, so he married Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim. Her unfaithfulness pictured Israel's unfaithfulness to God, and Hosea's continued love pictured God's love.

whyNot.D: Ruth married Boaz (Ruth 4:13).
whyNot.B: Abigail married David after Nabal's death (1 Samuel 25:39-42).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Hosea named his third child Lo-ammi. What message did this name carry for Israel?
options: God would have mercy on the house of Judah
God would soon destroy the house of Jehu at Jezreel
Israel would return from exile in seventy years
Israel was no longer to be called God's people
questions.explanation: Lo-ammi means 'not my people'. In Hosea 1:9 God said, 'You are not my people, and I am not your God,' because of Israel's unfaithfulness. Yet Hosea 1:10 goes on to promise that they would again be called children of the living God.

whyNot.B: The judgement on the house of Jehu is linked to the first son, Jezreel (Hosea 1:4).
whyNot.A: Mercy on Judah is mentioned with the daughter Lo-ruhamah (Hosea 1:7), whose name means 'no mercy' for Israel.
whyNot.C: Seventy years of exile is from Jeremiah's prophecy (Jeremiah 29:10).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: In Isaiah's vision in the temple, one of the seraphim touched his lips with a burning coal from the altar. What did this mean?
options: He would be burned for speaking falsely
He was being made king over Judah
His guilt was taken away and his sin forgiven
He would no longer be able to speak
questions.explanation: Isaiah cried that he was lost, a man of unclean lips (Isaiah 6:5). The seraph touched his mouth with the coal and said his guilt was taken away and his sin atoned for (Isaiah 6:7). Cleansed, Isaiah answered God's call: 'Here am I! Send me' (Isaiah 6:8).

whyNot.A: The coal cleansed Isaiah; it was not a punishment.
whyNot.D: Isaiah went on to speak God's message, so the coal did not silence him.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: God sent Jeremiah to the potter's house, where a spoiled pot was reworked into another vessel. What did this teach?
options: God had finally rejected the potters of Jerusalem
Clay pots should not be used in the temple
God can reshape a nation as He wills, depending on its response
Judah should take up pottery as a trade in exile
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 18:1-10 God said that as clay is in the potter's hand, so Israel is in His hand. If a nation turns from evil, God will relent of the disaster He planned; if it does evil, He will relent of the good. The lesson is God's sovereignty and the call to repent.

whyNot.D: The potter was a picture for God, not advice about a trade.
whyNot.A: The message concerns the nation, not the potters themselves.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: In Ezekiel's vision, the dry bones in the valley came together and lived. According to Ezekiel 37:11, what did the bones stand for?
options: The false prophets who misled the people
The whole house of Israel in exile, feeling hopeless
The Babylonians who would be judged by God
The soldiers who died when Jerusalem fell
questions.explanation: God told Ezekiel that the bones were the whole house of Israel, who were saying their bones were dried up and their hope was lost (Ezekiel 37:11). The vision promised that God would put His Spirit in them and bring them back to their own land.

whyNot.D: The bones were a symbol of the nation's hopeless state, not literally the war dead.
whyNot.C: The vision is a promise of restoration for Israel, not judgement on Babylon.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: The exiles quoted a proverb: 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.' How did Ezekiel answer it?
options: Each person will die for his own sin, not for his father's
Only the priests are responsible for the sins of the nation
God punishes sin only up to the third generation
Children will always be punished for their fathers' sins
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 18 God says the proverb will no longer be used. The soul who sins shall die; the son will not bear the guilt of the father, nor the father the guilt of the son (Ezekiel 18:20). This is Ezekiel's teaching on individual responsibility, and it urges everyone to repent and live.

whyNot.D: This is the very idea the proverb expressed and Ezekiel rejected.
whyNot.C: This is not Ezekiel's answer; Ezekiel 18 stresses that each person answers for his own deeds.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: What gifts did the wise men from the East present to the child Jesus?
options: Gold, a lamb and a dove
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:11 says the wise men entered the house, saw the child with Mary his mother, worshipped him and opened their treasures, offering gold, frankincense and myrrh.

whyNot.C: A pair of doves or pigeons was the offering Mary and Joseph gave at the temple (Luke 2:24), not a gift of the wise men.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: At the baptism of Jesus in the river Jordan, what happened as he came up from the water?
options: The Spirit descended like a dove and a voice called him God's beloved Son
John the Baptist was taken up into heaven
Fire came down and consumed the water
Moses and Elijah appeared and talked with him
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:16-17 says the heavens were opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove and rested on Jesus, and a voice from heaven said, 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.'

whyNot.D: Moses and Elijah appeared at the Transfiguration (Matthew 17:3), not at the baptism.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: When the devil tempted the hungry Jesus to turn stones into bread, how did Jesus reply?
options: Get behind me, Satan, for you are a hindrance
Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word from God
You shall not put the Lord your God to the test
My food is to do the will of Him who sent me
questions.explanation: In Matthew 4:3-4 Jesus answered the first temptation by quoting Deuteronomy 8:3: man does not live by bread alone but by every word that comes from the mouth of God. He put obedience to God above meeting his own physical need.

whyNot.C: This was his reply to the second temptation, to throw himself from the pinnacle of the temple (Matthew 4:7).
whyNot.A: Jesus said this to Peter (Matthew 16:23), not during the temptation.
whyNot.D: Jesus said this to his disciples at the well in Samaria (John 4:34).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: According to John's Gospel, what was the first of the signs Jesus performed?
options: Healing the official's son at Capernaum
Raising Lazarus from the dead at Bethany
Feeding five thousand people with five loaves
Turning water into wine at a wedding in Cana
questions.explanation: John 2:1-11 tells how the wine ran out at a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus had six stone jars filled with water, and it became good wine. John 2:11 calls this the first of his signs, by which he manifested his glory and his disciples believed in him.

whyNot.A: John 4:54 calls the healing of the official's son the second sign.
whyNot.B: Raising Lazarus came near the end of Jesus' ministry (John 11).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Nicodemus came to Jesus by night. What did Jesus tell him was necessary to see the kingdom of God?
options: He must offer a sacrifice in the temple
He must keep the law of Moses more strictly
He must be born again, of water and the Spirit
He must sell all he had and give to the poor
questions.explanation: Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews (John 3:1). Jesus told him that unless one is born again (born from above), of water and the Spirit, he cannot see or enter the kingdom of God (John 3:3-5). This new birth is a spiritual change brought by God.

whyNot.D: Jesus told the rich young man to sell what he had (Matthew 19:21), not Nicodemus.
whyNot.B: Nicodemus already kept the law as a Pharisee; Jesus pointed him to spiritual rebirth.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: In which district did Peter declare, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God'?
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:13-16 says that when Jesus came into the district of Caesarea Philippi he asked his disciples who people said he was, and then who they said he was. Simon Peter answered that he was the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus called him blessed, because this had been revealed by the Father.

whyNot.D: Capernaum was the base of Jesus' Galilean ministry, but the confession happened near Caesarea Philippi.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Jesus told the parable of the Good Samaritan in reply to a lawyer's question. What was that question?
options: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar?
How many times should I forgive my brother?
Which is the greatest of the prophets?
questions.explanation: In Luke 10:25-29 a lawyer agreed that the law requires love of God and of one's neighbour, then, wanting to justify himself, asked, 'And who is my neighbour?' Jesus told of a Samaritan who helped a wounded traveller whom a priest and a Levite passed by (Luke 10:30-37), showing that a neighbour is anyone in need whom we can help.

whyNot.B: Peter asked about forgiving his brother (Matthew 18:21), which led to the parable of the unforgiving servant.
whyNot.A: The question about taxes was put by Pharisees and Herodians (Matthew 22:15-17).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: After Jesus visited his house in Jericho, Zacchaeus said he would give half his goods to the poor. What else did he promise?
options: To restore fourfold to anyone he had defrauded
To leave his work and follow Jesus to Jerusalem
To build a synagogue for the people of Jericho
To offer a sacrifice for his sins at the temple
questions.explanation: Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector who was rich. In Luke 19:8 he said he would give half his goods to the poor and, if he had defrauded anyone, restore it fourfold. Jesus said salvation had come to his house, for the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost (Luke 19:9-10).

whyNot.C: Building a synagogue is linked to the centurion of Capernaum (Luke 7:5), not Zacchaeus.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: Who was compelled by the soldiers to carry the cross of Jesus on the way to Golgotha?
questions.explanation: Mark 15:21 says the soldiers compelled a passer-by, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, who was coming in from the country, to carry Jesus' cross. They brought Jesus to Golgotha, which means 'place of a skull' (Mark 15:22).

whyNot.C: Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate for Jesus' body and buried it (Mark 15:43-46).
whyNot.A: Simon Peter had denied Jesus and was not the one who carried the cross.
whyNot.B: Nicodemus helped Joseph with the burial (John 19:39).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: On the road to Emmaus, the risen Jesus walked with two disciples who did not recognise him. One of them is named in Luke 24. Who was he?
questions.explanation: Luke 24:13-18 tells of two disciples going to Emmaus, a village about seven miles from Jerusalem. Jesus joined them, and one of them, named Cleopas, asked him if he was the only visitor who did not know what had happened. They recognised Jesus when he broke bread with them (Luke 24:30-31).

whyNot.B: Thomas doubted the resurrection until Jesus appeared to him in Jerusalem (John 20:24-29).
whyNot.D: Matthias was chosen later to replace Judas (Acts 1:26).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: What happened to the disciples on the day of Pentecost, as recorded in Acts 2?
options: They saw Jesus taken up into heaven in a cloud
They were arrested and beaten by the council
They were filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke in other tongues
They chose Matthias to replace Judas
questions.explanation: Acts 2:1-4 says that when the day of Pentecost had come, a sound like a mighty wind filled the house, divided tongues as of fire rested on each of them, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues.

whyNot.A: The ascension took place before Pentecost (Acts 1:9).
whyNot.D: Matthias was chosen before Pentecost (Acts 1:26).

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: How was Matthias chosen to take the place of Judas Iscariot among the apostles?
options: The Jewish council elected him by vote
The apostles prayed and cast lots, and the lot fell on him
Jesus named him before the ascension
Peter appointed him because he was a close friend
questions.explanation: Acts 1:21-26 says the replacement had to be someone who had been with them from John's baptism to the ascension. Two men were put forward, Joseph called Barsabbas (Justus) and Matthias. The apostles prayed and cast lots, and the lot fell on Matthias.

whyNot.A: The council opposed the apostles; it played no part in choosing Matthias.
whyNot.C: Matthias was chosen after the ascension, in Jerusalem.

questions.subject: christian-religious-studies
questions.stem: At the temple gate called Beautiful, Peter told a man lame from birth that he had no silver or gold. What did Peter then do?
options: He sent him to the apostles to receive alms
He healed him in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth
He took him to the priests to be declared clean
He laid hands on him to receive the Holy Spirit
