questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The Action Group grew out of which Yoruba cultural organisation?
questions.explanation: Egbe Omo Oduduwa, a Yoruba cultural association founded by Awolowo and others in the 1940s, provided the base for the Action Group in 1951.

whyNot.D: Jam'iyyar Mutanen Arewa was the northern cultural body from which the NPC grew.
whyNot.C: The Ibo State Union was an Igbo cultural body linked to the NCNC.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The Northern Elements Progressive Union (NEPU), which opposed the NPC in the North, was led by
questions.explanation: Mallam Aminu Kano led NEPU, formed in 1950. It spoke for the common people (talakawa) against the power of the emirs and allied with the NCNC.

whyNot.D: Ahmadu Bello led the NPC, NEPU's rival.
whyNot.C: Joseph Tarka led the United Middle Belt Congress (UMBC).

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The National Congress of British West Africa, formed in 1920 to demand reforms such as elected representation, was led by
questions.explanation: J. E. Casely Hayford, a lawyer from the Gold Coast, led the National Congress of British West Africa. Its demands helped push Britain towards the elective principle in the Clifford Constitution of 1922.

whyNot.C: Macaulay led the NNDP in Lagos; the Congress was led from the Gold Coast.
whyNot.A: Nkrumah became prominent only in the late 1940s.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The Willink Commission (1957–58) was set up to look into
options: the fears of ethnic minorities and how to allay them
the causes of the 1945 general strike
the causes of the Aba Women's War
the results of the 1959 federal election
questions.explanation: Minority groups in each region feared domination by the major groups and asked for new states. The Willink Commission did not recommend new states but proposed that fundamental human rights be written into the constitution.

whyNot.D: The commission reported before the 1959 election took place.
whyNot.C: The Aba Women's War was in 1929, long before the commission.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: Why did Northern leaders oppose the 1953 motion for self-government in 1956?
options: The North had already become independent
The British had banned all political parties in the North
They wanted the North to join French West Africa
They felt the North was not yet ready, partly because it lagged behind in Western education
questions.explanation: NPC leaders feared that with fewer Western-educated people, the North would be dominated by the South in an early self-government. They proposed self-government 'as soon as practicable', and the North became self-governing only in 1959.

whyNot.A: No part of Nigeria was independent before 1960.
whyNot.B: The NPC itself was a legal northern party in the House.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: Who declared the Eastern Region an independent 'Republic of Biafra' in May 1967?
questions.explanation: Lt Col. Ojukwu, the military governor of the Eastern Region, declared Biafra on 30 May 1967. The civil war followed from July 1967 to January 1970.

whyNot.C: Gowon was the federal head of state who fought to keep Nigeria one.
whyNot.B: Effiong took over from Ojukwu at the end and announced Biafra's surrender in 1970.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: After the civil war, Gowon's programme of the '3Rs' stood for reconciliation, rehabilitation and
questions.explanation: The 3Rs were reconciliation (bringing people back together), rehabilitation (helping those affected) and reconstruction (rebuilding damaged areas), in line with the 'no victor, no vanquished' policy.

whyNot.C: Regionalism belongs to the Richards Constitution of 1946, not the post-war programme.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: Who was sworn in as President on 29 May 1999, at the start of the Fourth Republic?
questions.explanation: General Abdulsalami Abubakar's military government handed over power to Chief Olusegun Obasanjo of the PDP on 29 May 1999, beginning the Fourth Republic.

whyNot.A: Abdulsalami Abubakar was the military head of state who handed over.
whyNot.C: Yar'Adua became President in 2007.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: In 1976 the Murtala Mohammed government increased the number of states in Nigeria from 12 to
questions.explanation: In February 1976 Murtala Mohammed created seven new states, bringing the total from 12 to 19. The same government decided to build a new federal capital at Abuja.

whyNot.D: 21 states existed after Babangida created two more in 1987.
whyNot.C: 36 states came in 1996 under Abacha.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The meeting of January 1967 held to settle the crisis between the Federal Military Government and the Eastern Region took place at Aburi in
questions.explanation: Nigeria's military leaders met at Aburi in Ghana in January 1967. They disagreed afterwards about what had been agreed, and the crisis led to secession and civil war.

whyNot.D: Ethiopia's Addis Ababa hosted OAU peace efforts during the war, not the Aburi meeting.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: Which head of state created six new states in 1996, bringing the total to 36?
questions.explanation: In October 1996 Abacha created six states (Bayelsa, Ebonyi, Ekiti, Gombe, Nasarawa and Zamfara), raising the number from 30 to 36.

whyNot.A: Babangida created states in 1987 and 1991, reaching 30.
whyNot.C: Abdulsalami Abubakar created no new states.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: In 1971 Nigeria joined which organisation, reflecting the growing importance of oil to its economy?
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) in 1971 as oil became its main export and source of government revenue.

whyNot.B: ECOWAS was founded in 1975.
whyNot.A: Nigeria was a founding member of the OAU in 1963.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The two political parties created by the Babangida administration for the transition to the Third Republic were the
questions.explanation: Babangida's government created the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and the National Republican Convention (NRC). Their candidates, Abiola and Tofa, contested the annulled election of 12 June 1993.

whyNot.A: The NPN and UPN were Second Republic parties (1979–83).
whyNot.B: The NCNC and AG were First Republic parties.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The only region created in the First Republic through the procedure laid down in the constitution, in 1963, was the
questions.explanation: The Mid-Western Region was carved out of the Western Region in 1963 after a referendum, following the constitutional procedure. It became Bendel State in 1976.

whyNot.D: The Eastern Region was one of the original three regions from 1946.
whyNot.B: Rivers was created as a state in 1967 by military decree, not as a region.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The War Against Indiscipline (WAI) was launched in 1984 by the military government headed by
questions.explanation: The Buhari–Idiagbon government, which came to power on 31 December 1983, launched WAI in 1984 to promote orderliness, such as queuing, punctuality and a clean environment.

whyNot.A: Obasanjo's military government ended in 1979.
whyNot.C: Abacha came to power in 1993.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: Where is the headquarters of the ECOWAS Commission?
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Commission (formerly the Executive Secretariat) is based in Abuja, Nigeria's capital.

whyNot.A: ECOWAS was founded by a treaty signed in Lagos, but its headquarters is in Abuja.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: In which year was the United Nations Organisation founded?
questions.explanation: The UN was founded in 1945, at the end of the Second World War, to maintain world peace. Nigeria joined it in 1960 after independence.

whyNot.B: 1919 relates to the League of Nations after the First World War.
whyNot.C: 1960 is when Nigeria joined the UN.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was formed in Addis Ababa in
questions.explanation: The OAU was founded on 25 May 1963 in Addis Ababa by independent African states. 25 May is still marked as Africa Day.

whyNot.D: 1975 is when ECOWAS was founded.
whyNot.B: 2002 is when the African Union replaced the OAU.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth in 1995 after the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists under the military government of
questions.explanation: The executions in November 1995 under Abacha's regime caused international outrage, and the Commonwealth suspended Nigeria. It was restored after the return to civil rule in 1999.

whyNot.D: Babangida left office in 1993.
whyNot.A: Buhari's military government ended in 1985.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: ECOMOG, the ECOWAS peacekeeping force led largely by Nigeria, first intervened in 1990 in the civil war in
questions.explanation: ECOWAS set up ECOMOG in 1990 to stop the Liberian civil war. Nigeria provided most of the troops and money. ECOMOG later also served in Sierra Leone.

whyNot.A: Ghana contributed troops but did not have a civil war needing ECOMOG.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: Two heads of state given much credit for the founding of ECOWAS in 1975 were Yakubu Gowon of Nigeria and
questions.explanation: Gowon and Eyadéma of Togo worked together from the early 1970s to bring English- and French-speaking West African countries into one economic community, leading to the Treaty of Lagos in 1975.

whyNot.C: Nkrumah was overthrown in 1966 and died in 1972, before ECOWAS was formed.
whyNot.A: Tanzania is in East Africa and is not part of ECOWAS.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: When it was formed, the main aim of ECOWAS was to
options: promote economic co-operation and integration among member states
settle disputes between the Cold War superpowers
replace the national armies of members with one army
questions.explanation: ECOWAS was set up to promote economic co-operation: trade, free movement of people, and development across West Africa. Peacekeeping (ECOMOG) was added later.

whyNot.A: The fight against apartheid was mainly led through the OAU and the UN.
whyNot.D: ECOWAS never aimed to abolish national armies.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: In the 1961 plebiscite supervised by the United Nations, the people of the Northern Cameroons voted to
options: remain a trust territory under Britain
questions.explanation: The British Cameroons had been a UN trust territory administered with Nigeria. In 1961 the Northern Cameroons voted to join Nigeria, while the Southern Cameroons voted to join the Republic of Cameroon.

whyNot.D: It was the Southern Cameroons that chose to join Cameroon.
whyNot.A: Independence as a separate state was not one of the choices offered.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: Before the OAU was formed, Nigeria under Balewa belonged to the Monrovia Group, which favoured
options: an immediate union government for the whole of Africa
a military alliance with the Western powers
keeping colonial rule until all states were ready
gradual co-operation among African states that respected each state's sovereignty
questions.explanation: The Monrovia Group, including Nigeria and Liberia, wanted unity to grow gradually through economic and functional co-operation while each state kept its sovereignty. Nkrumah's Casablanca Group wanted immediate political union.

whyNot.A: Immediate union was the position of the Casablanca Group.
whyNot.C: Both groups supported the end of colonial rule.

questions.subject: history
questions.stem: The Songhai Empire collapsed after its army was defeated in 1591 by invaders from
questions.explanation: A Moroccan army armed with firearms crossed the Sahara and defeated the Songhai army at Tondibi in 1591. Songhai broke up after this defeat.

whyNot.A: The Portuguese traded on the coast and did not invade Songhai.
whyNot.D: Mali had itself been overtaken by Songhai long before 1591.
